quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A prompt says that no refund may be issued before the customer's identity has been verified. The sentence appears once, at the start of a long session, and after many turns the system begins to skip it. What explains this, and where should the requirement live?

options.a: The model loses interest in a rule after a set number of turns, so the sentence is repeated in every user message of the whole session
options.b: The context window resets between turns, so each request must carry the whole conversation by hand
options.c: The sentence is too short to carry weight, so it is lengthened with examples of identity checks
options.d: Compaction replaces early messages with a summary, so a rule that must hold throughout goes in CLAUDE.md or a hook

explanation.d: The page says what compaction does (module 45, page 2): "Compaction replaces older messages with a summary, so specific instructions from early in the conversation may not be preserved."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the cause is compaction and not boredom, and the remedy is placement: "Put rules that must hold for the whole run in `CLAUDE.md`, or enforce them in a hook."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the window does not reset: "The context window does not reset between turns within a session."
explanation.c: Ruled out because more words are not the remedy, since a hook "runs on every call, and a prompt does not always"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A customer writes in one message that a refund is wanted on one order, an address has changed, and a charge appears twice. Nothing has been looked up yet, and the three concerns relate to an order, an address record and a card statement. Which two steps does the page give before any tool runs? (Select two.)

options.a: Pass the whole text to a person, since several concerns need human judgement
options.b: Work on them in parallel with the shared context they need
options.c: Run the three matters one after another in a single chain, so that each sees the previous conclusion
options.d: List the matters separately, each with its own question and result
options.e: Handle only the first matter and ask the customer to send the others separately

explanation.b: The coordinator lists the items before any tool runs so that each has its own question and its own result, and the guide asks it to "look into each of them in parallel with the shared context they need" (module 48, page 2).
explanation.d: The coordinator lists the items before any tool runs so that each has its own question and its own result, and the guide asks it to "look into each of them in parallel with the shared context they need" (module 48, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the coordinator "lists the items before any tool runs, so that each has its own question and its own result".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Share the facts, not the conclusions."
explanation.e: Ruled out because the point of listing first is that "none is lost behind another".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A refund-limit hook should govern only the coordinator, yet it also fires for subagents that call the same tool. How can it tell the two apart?

options.a: Read the identity fields in its input present only for nested workers
options.b: Use a matcher that names the coordinator in its pattern
options.c: Register the hook only in the coordinator's options file
options.d: Wait for a subagent stop event and undo the call afterwards

explanation.a: The page names the fields (module 49, page 1): "Hooks also run inside subagents, with an `agent_id` and an `agent_type` in the input (module 47), so a hook that must apply only to the coordinator has to look at those fields."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a matcher sees names only: "Matchers only match tool names, not file paths or other arguments."
explanation.c: Ruled out because subagents do run hooks: "Hooks also run inside subagents"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a call cannot be undone afterwards: "A post hook can tell the model that something went wrong. It cannot make the refund not have happened."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A gate refuses a refund because identity is not verified. A teammate suggests that the gate should run the verification itself and carry on. Why not?

options.a: A gate may only read state and can never call a backend service, whatever the rule of the system
options.b: Running it would double the cost of every refund request that the desk handles
options.c: Verification calls are blocked inside any hook or dispatcher by the platform
options.d: Only the end user can supply the code, so it should decline and state what is lacking

explanation.d: The page gives the reason (module 48, page 1): "the customer's identity code is something the model must obtain from the customer, so the gate refuses and says what is missing".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the gate does call the backend after its checks: "For every tool call the model asks for, it checks the prerequisites, and only then does it call the backend."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the point is honesty and a small gate: "That keeps the conversation honest and keeps the gate small."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the gate does not repair: "The gate does not repair the call."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. In a loop built on the SDK, which party should own the decision whether a refund call runs, and where does that decision live?

options.a: The code, in permissions and hooks that act before execution
options.b: The model, through the stop reason of its reply to the call
options.c: The model, by weighing the policy text in its prompt each turn
options.d: A person, through a question after each call

explanation.a: The page assigns the decision (module 45, page 1): "Permissions and hooks, before the tool executes".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the stop reason answers a different question: "The stop reason of its reply"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a model weighs text as advice: "Memory is advice with good delivery."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a hook runs on every call: "It runs on every call, and a prompt does not always"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A support server exposes cancel_order, hold_order and release_order, which take the same inputs and return the same shape and differ only in the verb. What does the page advise?

options.a: Keep three separate tools, because separate names always improve the choice for the model
options.b: Fold them into a single tool with an action parameter, so that the model has fewer names to confuse
options.c: Split each by customer segment so that no two descriptions can overlap in the index
options.d: Merge them with a tool that infers the verb from the user's message each time

explanation.b: The page gives the fix (module 52, page 1): "Group under one tool with an `action` parameter".
explanation.a: Ruled out because more is not better: "More tools don't always lead to better outcomes."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a tool is a unit of choice: "so the right number is the number of different decisions you want it"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a smarter merge is a larger change: "it is a larger change than a first step needs"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A tool retries a transient billing failure, and the response carries a retry-after wait. Which two statements follow the page? (Select two.)

options.a: Without a hint, the pause doubles from a base
options.b: A constant pause of one second keeps the pressure even
options.c: The computed schedule is kept even when a wait is named
options.d: The delay that the service names replaces the computed value for that attempt
options.e: The hint is ignored and the retry is made at once, since the failure may be a fluke

explanation.a: The page states it: "When the failure carries a wait (a rate limit with a `retry-after`), that value replaces the computed one for that attempt", and otherwise "The wait doubles from a base: 100, 200, 400 milliseconds" (module 53, page 2).
explanation.d: The page states it: "When the failure carries a wait (a rate limit with a `retry-after`), that value replaces the computed one for that attempt", and otherwise "The wait doubles from a base: 100, 200, 400 milliseconds" (module 53, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A constant wait keeps the pressure on a service that is already struggling".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "that value replaces the computed one for that attempt".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "The service's word first."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A refund tool keeps getting amounts in the wrong format, and the model apologises after a few corrections. What does the page advise during development?

options.a: Raise the retry bound so that the model corrects itself more often than it does now in each session
options.b: Ask the model in the prompt to stop apologising and keep trying until it succeeds
options.c: Write more detailed descriptions, and let the error name the field with an example value
options.d: Switch the field to free text so that no value can ever be rejected by the tool

explanation.c: The page quotes the documentation (module 53, page 2): "your best bet during development is to try the request again with more-detailed `description` values".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the model already retries a few times: it "will retry 2-3 times with corrections before apologizing to the user"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the message does the teaching: "A message that names the field and gives an example value"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a validation failure is repaired by one value: "A validation failure is repaired by changing one value"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A refund cap tool receives the boolean true as the amount in the model's call. The backend would accept the value without complaint, yet the cap check is meant to rely on whole numbers. What should the tool layer do?

options.a: Treat it as one unit and carry on with the cap check
options.b: Refuse it as malformed, with a result that says what is needed
options.c: Pass it through to the backend unchanged, as it accepts it
options.d: Round it to the nearest allowed value and move to the next step

explanation.b: The page lists the check (module 54, page 2): "an amount that is missing, a fraction, a string or a boolean is refused as a bad amount".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a cap needs a real quantity: "A cap needs a number"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the layer is code and judgement is not: "the model's own judgement is probabilistic, and the layer is code"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a refusal is a usable result: "Each refusal is a result that the agent can use (module 53): it says what is needed and who can give it"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A new engineer's session ignores the team rule that every endpoint validates its input. A senior engineer wrote the rule into the personal memory file in his home folder, and nothing in the repository carries it. Where should the rule go?

options.a: In the project's own instruction document, committed so that everyone receives it
options.b: In each engineer's home-folder file, since one exists for every developer
options.c: In a managed policy location, which applies to everyone on a machine and cannot be excluded
options.d: In a local-only note beside the project instructions that is kept out of version control

explanation.a: The page states the fix (module 57, page 1): "The rule goes in the project file, committed."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a personal file travels with its owner: "so a new teammate never receives it"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the question is whether the text travels with the code: "whether it travels with the repository"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a local note is private: "A note about one project that nobody else needs, such as a sandbox address, goes in `CLAUDE.local.md`"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A team's refund-issuing procedure is a skill with real side effects. Which frontmatter setting stops the model from deciding on its own that the time has come to run it?

options.a: user-invocable: false, which hides the slash entry from the person
options.b: allowed-tools with a narrow list, which prevents any other tool from being called by the skill
options.c: The flag that blocks automatic invocation, so only a person typing the name starts it
options.d: A description that tells the model to wait for confirmation before it starts

explanation.c: The page names the flag (module 58, page 1): "keeps the model from deciding by itself that the time has come".
explanation.a: Ruled out because that setting is for background knowledge: "Background knowledge that is no action, such as an explanation of a legacy system, is `user-invocable: false`."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a tool list is not a restriction: "the product treats it as a pre-approval: Edit and Write stay callable."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a description only helps the model find a skill: "For a skill Claude may invoke, the description is the only thing in context until it loads"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A support team adds examples to the prompt of its refund decision reviewer. Besides judgement, what else do the examples steer?

options.a: The tone of the wording only, which is why they should sound friendly
options.b: The length of the prompt, which is why they should be kept short
options.c: The language of the reply, which is why they should use the customer's own words
options.d: The format of the answer, which is why they should mirror the real output

explanation.d: The page states it (module 61, page 2): "They should also mirror the real output: show the format the answer must have, since examples are the surest way to steer format as well as judgement."
explanation.a: Ruled out because examples are for the border cases: "Few-shot examples are not a sample of typical cases; typical cases are already handled by the criteria."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a count is a sanity check: "the guide asks for two to four targeted examples, and a long list teaches accidents"
explanation.c: Ruled out because examples teach accidents of form: "five examples that all end with the same label teach the label"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. Which escalation triggers can the application itself check in code, without relying on the model's recollection?

options.a: The customer's mood, measured by a count of exclamation marks in the message
options.b: The model's own confidence in its answer, as it reports the number itself
options.c: Whether the issue sounds complicated to a reader of the transcript
options.d: Those that are plain facts, such as a spoken request for a person

explanation.d: The page states it (module 65, page 1): "can be checked by the application, which then does not rely on the model's recollection of an instruction".
explanation.a: Ruled out because mood is not on the list: "Sentiment, a count of exclamation marks and the model's own confidence are not on the list."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a self-reported number is not calibrated: "It is not calibrated to whether the case is within policy"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a feeling says little about the case: "none of them says whether the case is within what the agent may decide"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A developer's request sends only the newest customer message to the Messages API, and the reply reads as if the chat had just begun. Why?

options.a: Short messages are treated as new sessions by default in the platform
options.b: The reply is cached from the last request and replayed to the caller
options.c: The model resets its memory when a message is under ten words long
options.d: The platform stores no conversation, so each call must carry all the history it needs

explanation.d: The page states it (module 64, page 1): "The Messages API keeps no conversation: every request carries the whole history it needs".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a lone message gets answers as though it were the first: "a request that sends only the newest message gets answers as though it were the first message"
explanation.b: Ruled out because what to resend is a decision: "Trimming and summarising are therefore decisions about what to resend"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the window does not reset: "The context window does not reset between turns within a session."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A support chat must shrink its history, and its oldest message is a tool call whose result is the next message. How should the window cut?

options.a: Remove the pair as a unit, since half of an exchange is an invalid record
options.b: Drop only the call and keep the result, since the result holds the facts
options.c: Drop only the result and keep the call, since the call records the intent
options.d: Keep both and drop the newest message instead

explanation.a: The page states it (module 64, page 2): "The unit to drop is the exchange, not the message: a tool call and its result stay together or go together".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a lone result is invalid: "a result with no call (or a call with no result) is an invalid"
explanation.c: Ruled out because two rules keep a window valid: "Two rules keep it valid."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the oldest goes first: "keep the newest turns that fit the budget and drop the oldest"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A team plans to answer short factual look-ups from free-tier users with a coordinator and several helpers, because the published design does this. Each look-up is worth very little to the business. What is the sound objection?

options.a: Helpers cannot answer factual questions, since they work in isolated context
options.b: A coordinator can only delegate to helpers whose descriptions are written in code
options.c: Such arrangements cost many times the tokens of a chat, so they suit only tasks whose value pays for them
options.d: Several helpers on one question always produce conflicting answers that need a human referee

explanation.c: The article gives the price (module 46, page 1): "multi-agent systems use about 15× more tokens than chats", so the value has to pay for it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because isolation is not the obstacle: the page says what comes back, "the work is self-contained and can return a summary."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the coordinator chooses from natural-language descriptions: "Claude uses each subagent's description to decide when to delegate tasks."
explanation.d: Ruled out because conflict is not the objection, and the page ties effort to the question: "Simple fact-finding requires just 1 agent with 3-10 tool calls"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A research coordinator runs under a spending cap, and its subagents have used most of it. The cap is reached while two subagents are still working. Which two things happen in the Agent SDK? (Select two.)

options.a: The run is paused until the next billing period and then resumed
options.b: Starting another helper fails with a budget error
options.c: The running subagents finish, since only the coordinator's own calls count toward the cap
options.d: Background helpers stop and the query ends with a budget subtype
options.e: The cap is lowered for later subagents and the run continues on the remaining funds

explanation.b: Once the cap is reached, "spawning another subagent fails with `Budget limit reached`" and Claude Code stops any background subagents still running, and the query ends with the `error_max_budget_usd` subtype (module 46, page 2).
explanation.d: Once the cap is reached, "spawning another subagent fails with `Budget limit reached`" and Claude Code stops any background subagents still running, and the query ends with the `error_max_budget_usd` subtype (module 46, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because Claude Code "stops any background subagents still running" once the cap is reached.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the budget cap covers subagents: their spend counts toward the total."
explanation.e: Ruled out because a refused spawn is "a normal outcome of a run that spent its budget".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A research system must use only its own restricted subagents, but the coordinator sometimes starts the general-purpose one that comes with the SDK. The team defined three narrow specialists with limited abilities and wants no fallback to anything broader. Which setting prevents it?

options.a: A longer description on each custom definition, so that the model always prefers it to the built-in one
options.b: An allow rule for the Agent tool, which limits it to custom definitions
options.c: The environment variable that removes the bundled helper, after which such a call fails
options.d: A lower turn limit for the coordinator, so that it cannot reach the built-in one

explanation.c: The page names the switch (module 47, page 1): "Setting `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` removes the built-in agent, and such a call then fails with `subagent_type is required`."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a description steers the choice and does not remove the option: "Claude uses each subagent's description to decide when to delegate tasks."
explanation.b: Ruled out because an allow rule only skips approval: the Agent tool is among the tools "that don't ask before running", listed or not
explanation.d: Ruled out because a turn limit bounds a run and does not change which subagents exist; the page says "A team that must only ever use its own named, restricted subagents sets it, because the general-purpose agent has every tool."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A coordinator must run a style review, a security scan and a coverage check on one change, and then write a summary that uses all three results. How should it invoke the subagents?

options.a: Start them one at a time across separate turns, so that nothing conflicts
options.b: Start all four together, with the summary agent reading the others' files as they appear on disk
options.c: Start the summary agent first, so that it can ask the others for what it needs
options.d: Launch the three together in one response, then compose the closing brief from their reports

explanation.d: The page says when parallel fits (module 47, page 2): "independent subtasks finish in the time of the slowest one rather than the sum of all of them", and a part that needs the others' output comes after them.
explanation.a: Ruled out because independent parts gain from running together: "they finish in the time of the slowest when run together, and several calls in one coordinator response start them together."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a part that needs another's output is a sequence: "It does not fit when one part needs another's output: that is a sequence"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the summary needs the reports first: "Run dependent parts in sequence, and write the second brief with the first result."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A coordinator session runs in bypassPermissions for a batch job, and a reviewer definition sets permissionMode to plan. The job runs unattended overnight on a build server. In which mode does the reviewer run?

options.a: Plan, because the definition is more specific than the session that started the whole batch job
options.b: Full autonomy, because the parent's blanket approval carries over and a helper's own setting cannot narrow it
options.c: Default, because the SDK lowers a subagent's mode to the safest one that exists in the product
options.d: Plan, because a subagent may never run in a mode more permissive than its own definition

explanation.b: The page gives the rule (module 47, page 1): "A subagent runs in `bypassPermissions` mode only when the parent session itself does", and a definition's `permissionMode` applies only under a parent in `default`, `dontAsk` or `plan` mode.
explanation.a: Ruled out because specificity does not win: "A subagent runs in the parent session's permission mode unless you set `permissionMode` on its `AgentDefinition`"
explanation.c: Ruled out because nothing lowers the mode: "inheriting `bypassPermissions` grants them full, autonomous system access."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the definition does not cap the parent's mode: "An architect who runs the coordinator in a bypass mode for CI has also decided that for every subagent."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A coordinator's subagents keep spawning further subagents of their own, and the team wants to stop all nesting. Which setting does that?

options.a: Lower the maximum depth variable to one
options.b: Raise the concurrency variable to twenty, which limits spawn chains
options.c: Remove the Agent tool from the parent's allowed list
options.d: Set a budget cap so low that no deeper spawn can pay

explanation.a: The page gives the default (module 46, page 1): nesting reaches "up to three layers below the main conversation" unless the depth variable is lowered to one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because concurrency counts parallel workers and not depth: "at most 20 subagents run at once by default"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a tool left off the allowed list still exists: "a tool that is not listed still exists"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a budget counts spending: "the budget cap counts the subagents' spending toward the total"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A research system connects many servers, and the SDK's automatic mode counts the tokens of deferrable definitions against the window. When does tool search become active?

options.a: At half of the window, so that a lot of room stays for the conversation with the user
options.b: At ten percent of the context size, below which everything loads up front
options.c: As soon as a second server connects, whatever the token count
options.d: Only when a person turns it on in the settings file

explanation.b: The page states the threshold (module 52, page 2): "When the total reaches 10% of the window, tool search activates."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the threshold is low because accuracy drops early: "Tool selection accuracy degrades with more than 30-50 tools loaded at once."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the trigger is a token count: "counts the tokens of the definitions that can be deferred"
explanation.d: Ruled out because it is not a switch left to a person: "Tool search is on by default, with the exceptions listed in Configure tool search"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A research team needs a standard integration with a widely used service. Which does the guide prefer, and which kind of work still justifies a build of the team's own?

options.a: A custom server, since only an own build can be trusted with the credentials of the company
options.b: A custom server, so that its descriptions can be tuned to the model that uses it
options.c: Several overlapping servers, so that the agent can always choose the best one for the task
options.d: A reviewed existing connector, with fresh development kept for unique processes

explanation.d: The page states the preference (module 55, page 2): "For a standard integration the guide chooses an existing community server over a custom one, and keeps custom servers for team-specific workflows."
explanation.a: Ruled out because trust is checked for every server: "Verify you trust each server before connecting it."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the model reads names and descriptions of whatever exists: "The model picks a tool from its name and description"
explanation.c: Ruled out because overlap distracts: "Too many tools or overlapping tools can also distract agents from pursuing efficient strategies."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A team sets allowed_tools to Read and Grep for a writer subagent and expects that nothing else is available. What is true?

options.a: The rest is removed, since a list of allowed names is a whitelist that excludes whatever is omitted
options.b: The rest still exists, since the list only approves, and unlisted calls follow the permission mode
options.c: The rest is denied, since unlisted calls need a person to approve each one individually
options.d: The rest is hidden from the model, but can still run if the model insists on it

explanation.b: The page states it (module 54, page 1): "Any other tool not listed in `allowed_tools` is still available to Claude, and a call to it that needs approval falls through to the permission mode".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the name suggests more than the field does: "The restriction is real in the SDK, but it is not where the name suggests"
explanation.c: Ruled out because an unlisted call follows the mode: "a call to it that needs approval falls through to the permission mode"
explanation.d: Ruled out because removal is another control: "a bare tool name in `disallowedTools` removes the tool from the agent's context"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A skill with the setting context: fork is started from a research coordinator that has built up a long conversation. What does the forked subagent see?

options.a: A copy of the parent conversation, since a fork copies the history
options.b: The parent's tool results but not its messages
options.c: Its own instructions, which must therefore stand on their own
options.d: The summary that compaction produced for the parent

explanation.c: The page states it (module 58, page 2): "The subagent doesn't see your conversation history, so the skill's instructions have to stand on their own."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the name misleads: "The name misleads: this is not a fork of the conversation"
explanation.b: Ruled out because nothing of the parent is passed: "The subagent doesn't see your conversation history"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the prompt is the skill: it "gives it the skill content as its prompt"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A research system's extraction returns claims with sources. Which two statements are true of the check that lets code catch a claim that no source supports? (Select two.)

options.a: The model double-checks its own output and reports changes
options.b: The schema gives every field a minimum length of several words
options.c: Each assertion carries a verbatim quote, tested by plain substring
options.d: A grounded value is not thereby a correct one
options.e: The model reports its confidence in each claim, and low ones are dropped

explanation.c: "The check is a plain substring test in code: it does not ask the model whether it is right", and "Provenance does not prove a value is correct, only that it is grounded" (module 62, page 1).
explanation.d: "The check is a plain substring test in code: it does not ask the model whether it is right", and "Provenance does not prove a value is correct, only that it is grounded" (module 62, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a self-check "carries the same blind spot as the finding".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A length limit such as `minLength` is not the answer".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "the answer to a precision problem is explicit categories and examples, never an adjective about confidence".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A long report is extracted in chunks, and the figures of the chunks must be combined into one total. Who should add them?

options.a: The synthesis model, asked to add the figures
options.b: Ordinary code that recomputes the sum, never a model asked for arithmetic
options.c: The first chunk's extraction, which keeps its own total and never revises it
options.d: The last chunk's extraction, which keeps a running total

explanation.b: The page states it (module 62, page 2): "recompute the total in code, not by asking a model to add".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a model is not asked whether it is right: "it does not ask the model whether it is right"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the first value is kept for fields and not for totals: "keep the first value that is neither null nor unclear, with the quote it came with"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a different total is a conflict: "when a later chunk gives a different vendor or total, do not pick silently"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. Five topics were scheduled for research, and four were covered. The report leaves out the fifth. Which two statements describe what the coverage note does? (Select two.)

options.a: The topic is listed under no findings, since nothing was found for it
options.b: That section sets the plan against what happened
options.c: The topic is omitted, since the note covers only what was searched
options.d: Something never looked into is recorded as a gap
options.e: The topic is listed as partial, since part of the plan was carried out

explanation.b: "A topic that was never searched is a gap", and the note is "the place where the system's own plan is compared with what happened" (module 66, page 2).
explanation.d: "A topic that was never searched is a gap", and the note is "the place where the system's own plan is compared with what happened" (module 66, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "`No findings`: topics that were searched and have nothing".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A report that quietly omits a topic is saying something false by leaving it out".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "`Partial`: topics that rest on part of their sources, with the cause".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A pipeline wants every finding to carry a source. Where should a finding without one be refused?

options.a: At the point of entry, with the origin made part of the required schema
options.b: In the final report, where the writer drops the lines that lack a reference
options.c: At synthesis, where the model decides which findings are worth keeping
options.d: After publication, when a reader asks about the figure's origin

explanation.a: The page states it (module 69, page 1): "so that a finding without one is refused where it enters the pipeline, and not discovered in the final report".
explanation.b: Ruled out because sources cannot be rebuilt from prose: "the sources are lost in the compression and cannot be rebuilt from prose"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a prose hand-off drops attribution: "A single prose hand-off anywhere in the chain is where attribution drops out."
explanation.d: Ruled out because an unsourced statement is not returned as a finding: "A subagent that cannot name a source for a statement does not return it as a finding"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. One report is cited on two dates in a ledger, and no other source agrees with its figure. How is the claim classed in the coverage note?

options.a: Well supported, since two dates give two separate confirmations
options.b: Contested, since the same figure appears there with two dates
options.c: Changed, since a value was cited at different times in the ledger by the same publisher
options.d: As resting on a single origin, since a repeated citation counts once

explanation.d: The page states it (module 69, page 2): "\"At least two distinct sources\" counts source names: the same report cited on two dates is one source, and agreement needs independence."
explanation.a: Ruled out because well supported needs two sources: "`agreed`, and the value has at least two distinct sources"
explanation.b: Ruled out because contested means different values on one date: "Several values on the same date"
explanation.c: Ruled out because changed means different values on different dates: "Several values on different dates"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A guard script for Claude Code fails with an unhandled exception on unexpected input. What is the effect on the action it guards?

options.a: The call goes ahead, since a crash ends with status 1, which does not block
options.b: The call is blocked, because a crashed guard counts as a refusal
options.c: The whole session stops, because the crash is reported as a fatal error
options.d: The call is held until a person approves it, since a failed guard falls back to asking

explanation.a: The page names the trap (module 49, page 2): "an unhandled exception exits with 1, which does not block".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a crash looks like a refusal, and that is the trap: "It is tempting because a crash looks like a refusal"
explanation.c: Ruled out because for most events the result is mild: "the action goes ahead and a notice appears in the transcript"
explanation.d: Ruled out because nothing asks anyone: "A guard that crashes on unexpected input is therefore a guard that lets the call through."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A CI session must not end its turn while the tests still fail, and a request in the prompt has not been reliable. Which control is stronger?

options.a: A hook on the stop event that runs the suite and keeps the run open until it passes
options.b: A stronger sentence at the end of the prompt asking for passing results
options.c: A larger turn limit so that the model has time to fix the failures
options.d: A second model call that confirms whether the output looks done

explanation.a: The page names the control (module 71, page 2): a Stop hook "blocks the turn from ending until it passes".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a model stops when the work looks done: "Claude stops when the work looks done"
explanation.c: Ruled out because time does not add a check: "A longer job timeout only lets a loop run longer."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a judgement is not a gate: "a decision made on prose is a guess"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A developer adds a server named github in the local scope with another URL than the project file's entry of that name. Which definition does Claude Code end up using?

options.a: Both, in turn, since each definition is treated as a separate server by the client
options.b: Once, using the private version, since the highest-ranking source wins whole and no blending occurs
options.c: The project's entry, since a shared definition always outranks a private one on a team
options.d: A merge of the two, taking the URL from one entry and the headers from the other entry

explanation.b: The page states it (module 55, page 1): "Claude Code connects to it once, using the definition from the highest-precedence source."
explanation.a: Ruled out because it connects once: "Claude Code connects to it once"
explanation.c: Ruled out because local ranks first: "The order is local, project, user, plugin-provided servers, then claude.ai connectors."
explanation.d: Ruled out because fields are not merged: "fields are not merged across scopes"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. Each item from a review becomes an inline comment with its file, line, severity and fix. Which extra field lets the team tune its criteria?

options.a: A free-text apology field that softens the tone of every comment
options.b: A hash of the whole diff so that duplicate comments can be removed later
options.c: A label naming the detected pattern per entry, so dismissals can be analysed
options.d: The reviewer's temperature setting, so that separate runs can be compared with one another

explanation.c: The page names the field (module 60, page 2): "a `detected_pattern` field per finding lets the team analyse which patterns draw dismissals and tune the criteria".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the comment already has its fields: "each finding becomes an inline comment with its file, line, severity and suggested fix"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the prompt carries the history: "A record of findings between runs, which the prompt carries, is the only state the pipeline has."
explanation.d: Ruled out because repeating does not help: "Retrying inside the job repeats cost with no reason to expect a different result"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A CI step sometimes loops for an hour, and its prompt already asks it to be quick. Which two controls does the page give? (Select two.)

options.a: A second sentence in the prompt names the minutes it may use
options.b: An environment variable switches on a quick mode
options.c: The tools that run without asking are listed on the command
options.d: A turn limit on the command ends the run
options.e: A longer job timeout gives the loop room to end itself

explanation.c: "`--max-turns` stops a loop, and `--allowedTools` lists what runs without asking, because nobody can approve a prompt" (module 74, page 1).
explanation.d: "`--max-turns` stops a loop, and `--allowedTools` lists what runs without asking, because nobody can approve a prompt" (module 74, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A prompt that asks the run to be quick is a request, not a limit."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "There is no headless environment variable and no `--batch` flag on the command line".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "A longer job timeout only lets a loop run longer."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A review of forty files in one pass gives detailed notes for some and a glance for others, and a team proposes a model with a larger window for the same pass. What is the verdict?

options.a: Repeat the single pass three times and keep what two runs agree upon
options.b: More room does not restore attention, so split the work per item and add a cross stage
options.c: Keep one pass but ask the reviewer to take equal care with every file
options.d: Lower the number of findings requested so that each file gets a longer note

explanation.b: The page states it (module 74, page 2): "a larger context window does not fix attention quality".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the remedy fits the cause: "The remedy that fits the cause is to divide the work."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a request for care is not a mechanism: "A sentence that asks for more care is a request"
explanation.d: Ruled out because attention thins with the number of files: "attention thins as the number of files in one pass grows"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. An unattended pipeline gives its code-checking job a shell because it sometimes runs git. Why is that a finding?

options.a: Reading and searching suffice, so nothing able to change files should be listed
options.b: A shell is slower than the file tools and delays the job
options.c: A shell cannot be restricted by allowed-tools patterns in a pipeline
options.d: A shell is needed for the job to read the diff, so it must stay

explanation.a: The page states it (module 74, page 2): "A shell tool is a way to change things, and a pipeline that nobody watches should not hold one for a job that only reads."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the point is capability and not speed: "A review changes nothing, so its tools are `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`"
explanation.c: Ruled out because patterns do restrict: "`Bash(git tag *)` pre-approves `git tag v1.2.0` and not `git push --force`"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the diff arrives another way: "The diff goes in on standard input or in the prompt."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A headless review step runs in a workflow with no interactive login. Which two statements describe how it should be set up? (Select two.)

options.a: The key is written into the workflow file as a literal so that every runner has it
options.b: The key is read from the developer's subscription login in the runner's keychain
options.c: The key is passed in the prompt so that the model can attach it to its requests
options.d: The tool list is complete and minimal, with read tools and no bare shell
options.e: The API key comes from a repository secret exposed as an environment variable

explanation.d: A bare run needs the key in the environment, "in the workflow that is a secret reference, never a literal", and "the tool list must be complete and minimal: read tools for a review, and no bare `Bash`" (module 60, page 1).
explanation.e: A bare run needs the key in the environment, "in the workflow that is a secret reference, never a literal", and "the tool list must be complete and minimal: read tools for a review, and no bare `Bash`" (module 60, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "in the workflow that is a secret reference, never a literal".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "because it does not use a subscription login".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A credential is a reference, never a value and never a default."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A CI runner relies on notes that Claude wrote to its auto memory on a developer's laptop. Will the runner have them?

options.a: Yes, since auto memory is committed with the repository
options.b: Yes, since it is synced through the cloud account for every session
options.c: Only the first 200 lines are synced, and the rest stays local
options.d: No, since those entries stay on the host that produced them

explanation.d: The page states it (module 57, page 1): the files "are not shared across machines or cloud environments".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the notes live in the home folder: "Claude writes its own notes to `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`"
explanation.b: Ruled out because they stay on the machine: "keeps them on the machine"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the 200 lines are a load limit: "the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A team asks what line count the documentation gives as the target for a root memory file, since its practice exercise sets a much lower limit for a small project.

options.a: Twenty-five lines, which the documentation sets for projects of a small size
options.b: Roughly two hundred, whereas the stricter cap is a testing choice
options.c: Five hundred lines, the ceiling the documentation names
options.d: No target at all, as it leaves the length to each team

explanation.b: The page states it (module 71, page 1): "The documented target is 200."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the lower figure is the course's: "That number is the course's, chosen to make the point testable."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the root file loads at launch: "The root `CLAUDE.md` and the rule files without a `paths` list load at the start of every session"
explanation.d: Ruled out because length dilutes guidance: "A word on dilution, which the guide names as a reason to keep files short"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A team adds minLength to a required field to stop placeholder strings. Why does that not work?

options.a: Placeholder strings tend to be longer than real values, so the limit rejects real ones
options.b: A length limit applies to optional fields and not to required ones
options.c: Decoding does not enforce it, and size cannot tell a real value from an invented one
options.d: The model ignores each constraint in a schema, whatever its kind

explanation.c: The page states it (module 62, page 1): "A length limit such as `minLength` is not the answer: constrained decoding does not enforce it (it is on the list of unsupported constraints), and it would not tell a real number from an invented one."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a placeholder looks like data: "And do not give a default that looks like data (`PO-0000`, `unknown`): downstream code cannot tell it from a real value."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the remedy is in the schema: "a field that may be missing from the source is optional or nullable"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the schema has to stay within what is supported: "Keep to the features structured outputs support"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A team puts a tool-using review into a batch. Which two results are possible? (Select two.)

options.a: An entry may come back as a call to run something
options.b: A multi-round procedure runs live, or each round becomes its own entry later
options.c: The entry is refused at submission, since batches take no tools
options.d: The entry streams partial answers that the client reassembles
options.e: An entry returns a finished answer, since a batch runs the tools itself

explanation.a: "A request that offers tools may come back with a tool call as its answer", and a workflow that needs several rounds with tools "therefore runs synchronously, or is cut so that each round is its own entry in successive batches" (module 63, page 1).
explanation.b: "A request that offers tools may come back with a tool call as its answer", and a workflow that needs several rounds with tools "therefore runs synchronously, or is cut so that each round is its own entry in successive batches" (module 63, page 1).
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Tools, system prompts, earlier turns and extended thinking are allowed."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the results come back as one file, not a stream".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "In a synchronous loop your code would run the tool and send the result in the next request".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A developer at the keyboard asks for a review but names neither a branch nor a reviewer. Which handling does the page prefer for an attended session?

options.a: Ask about every missing detail before doing anything
options.b: Stop with a plain failure that lists the missing fields
options.c: Proceed silently on guesses, so that the developer is not interrupted
options.d: Ask only what cannot be assumed, and state the assumptions

explanation.d: The page states it (module 61, page 2): "to state the assumptions made for the rest".
explanation.a: Ruled out because questions are for what cannot be assumed: "ask only what cannot be assumed"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a failure belongs to the unattended case: "In an unattended run (CI) nobody can answer, so it never asks: it proceeds on stated assumptions where a default exists, and stops with a clear failure where a required field has none."
explanation.c: Ruled out because silence is not acceptable: "A job never passes by saying nothing."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A CI extraction step fails the sum check and is retried. What must the second request hold besides the original document?

options.a: The faulty record and the specific errors with their fields
options.b: Nothing more, since the same request gets a new sample each time it is sent again
options.c: Only the error message, to keep the request short
options.d: A note asking the model to try harder

explanation.a: The page states it (module 62, page 2): "The request on the second attempt holds three things: the original document, the failed record, and the specific errors".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a repeat gets the same result: "A retry that repeats the request gets the same answer with the same probability."
explanation.c: Ruled out because what went wrong is the useful part: "A retry that carries what went wrong gives the model something to correct."
explanation.d: Ruled out because some values cannot be supplied by any retry: "a retry cannot supply it and may fabricate it"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. Six exploring workers may be lost to a crash. When should the coordinator write each worker's manifest entry?

options.a: When the worker finishes, so that the entry shows a final status for it in the ledger of the run
options.b: At launch of each one, so that an abrupt stop leaves a trace of what began
options.c: After each worker's last message, together with its closing summary
options.d: Once at the end of the whole job, rebuilt from the logs of all runs

explanation.b: The page states it (module 67, page 2): "It writes an agent's entry when the agent starts, so that a crash leaves a trace of work that began and has nothing to show."
explanation.a: Ruled out because state is written as the work goes: "It is written as the agent learns and not only at the end, so that a crash half-way leaves something."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a crash gives no warning: "A crash does not warn."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the manifest is small and readable: "The manifest is small, readable by a person"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A fan-out extraction pass receives a document that holds only blank pages. What should the run do?

options.a: Send it with a note that it is empty so that the model can confirm that
options.b: Not send it, because a call with nothing to examine only costs money
options.c: Send it anyway and discard whatever comes back from the model
options.d: Split it into parts so that each part can be checked separately

explanation.b: The page states it (module 50, page 2): "A file of blank lines is not sent at all."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a call with nothing to read still costs: "A call with nothing to review costs money"
explanation.c: Ruled out because an answer to nothing would reach the next pass: "because a summary that is empty or invented would be read as"
explanation.d: Ruled out because splitting is for long files: "A file that does not fit a pass of its own is cut into parts of a fixed number of lines"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. An extraction pass is limited to 200 lines per call, and a document has exactly 200 lines. Which two statements follow the page? (Select two.)

options.a: The document is cut into two parts, since the final line needs its own
options.b: The document is refused, since one at the limit counts as too long
options.c: Only a file too long for one run is cut
options.d: The document is cut into two parts that overlap by one line
options.e: A file as long as the maximum is one part, not two

explanation.c: The page states it: "A file that is exactly as long as the limit is one part, not two", and a file is cut only when "A file that does not fit a pass of its own is cut into parts of a fixed number of lines" (module 50, page 2).
explanation.e: The page states it: "A file that is exactly as long as the limit is one part, not two", and a file is cut only when "A file that does not fit a pass of its own is cut into parts of a fixed number of lines" (module 50, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A file that is exactly as long as the limit is one part, not two."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A file that does not fit a pass of its own is cut into parts of a fixed number of lines", and this one fits.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The parts do not overlap, so a finding is not reported twice."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A post-call hook converts amounts from cents to decimals and dates to a readable form. A result also holds a field that the hook's table does not list. What should the hook do with it?

options.a: Drop it, so that the model sees just the fields the hook knows
options.b: Convert it with the closest rule, to keep the output uniform
options.c: Block the call, since an unknown field means that something failed
options.d: Pass it through as it was, since a normaliser changes only what it understands

explanation.d: The page states the rule (module 49, page 2): "Fields that are not in the table pass through as they were."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a normaliser changes only what it understands: "Change only what you understand."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a readable value is left as it is: "A value that is already readable is not touched"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a post hook cannot stop anything: "It cannot make the refund not have happened."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. An extraction tool rejects a date given as next Friday. Which two statements describe the reply that lets the model repair its input? (Select two.)

options.a: It is a success with an empty field, so that the next stage asks again
options.b: It is a transient error with retry set, since the user may type again
options.c: The message names the format to use
options.d: It is a protocol error with a generic code, since the form was malformed
options.e: It is a flagged execution error in the validation category

explanation.c: The page classifies it: "an input validation failure, so a tool execution error with the flag, and the message can say which format to use" (module 53, page 1).
explanation.e: The page classifies it: "an input validation failure, so a tool execution error with the flag, and the message can say which format to use" (module 53, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Write instructive error messages."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The input was wrong: a missing field, a value out of range, a bad format".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A request that names a tool the server does not have is a protocol error, since there is nothing to run."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A field accepts only open, shipped or closed. How should the tool schema express it?

options.a: As a sentence in the description that lists the three allowed words
options.b: As a free string, validated by the pipeline after the call returns
options.c: As an enum, so the model sees the allowed values and strict use refuses others
options.d: As a number code that the model must remember from the prompt text

explanation.c: The page gives the benefit (module 52, page 1): "The model sees the allowed values in the schema, and a strict tool (module 26) refuses the others."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the schema carries what a script can check: "The schema carries what a script can check"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the schema is where syntax is removed: "The schema: constrained decoding or strict tool use"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the model reads the schema each time: "A tool is therefore a name, a description and a schema, and the model reads all three each time it decides."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A third-party extraction server marks its delete_record tool as read-only, and a team plans to let the agent call it without confirmation on that basis. What is the objection?

options.a: Read-only hints are ignored by the SDK, which treats every integration as writable by default
options.b: Hints are verified by the client against the handler, so a false one is caught
options.c: Such hints are the vendor's claim and count as untrusted unless the source is trusted
options.d: Read-only hints exist only for built-in tools and cannot be set by a server

explanation.c: The page cites the specification (module 52, page 2): "MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the SDK does use the hint: "The Agent SDK uses the hints in one place"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a hint is not checked against the handler: "A tool marked `readOnlyHint: true` can still write to disk if that's what the handler does."
explanation.d: Ruled out because servers do set them: "Optional properties describing tool behavior"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A skill that extracts fields from documents sets context: fork and names no agent. Which subagent type runs it?

options.a: The Explore one, which is limited to read-only search
options.b: A new subagent that inherits the parent's conversation
options.c: None, as a forked skill needs a named agent first
options.d: The general-purpose one, which is the default

explanation.d: The page states it (module 58, page 2): "`context: fork` starts a new subagent of the type named in `agent` (the default is `general-purpose`)".
explanation.a: Ruled out because Explore is a separate built-in: "Claude Code ships an Explore subagent for exactly this work"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a forked skill sees no history: "The subagent doesn't see your conversation history"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a default exists: "the default is `general-purpose`"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A skill body uses $1, and the user types only one argument. What does the second placeholder become?

options.a: It stays in the text, where a named one expands to nothing
options.b: An empty string in the place of the missing second argument
options.c: The first argument repeated in the second slot of the text
options.d: The full list of arguments joined together into a single string

explanation.a: The page states it (module 58, page 2): an indexed placeholder with no argument "stays in the content unchanged".
explanation.b: Ruled out because that is the behaviour of a named placeholder: "while a named one expands to an empty string"
explanation.c: Ruled out because indexes count from zero and do not wrap: "The argument at index N, counting from 0"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the full list belongs to another placeholder: "All arguments, as typed"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A document gives a currency that the closed enum does not list, and another document leaves the currency unstated. Which enum design handles both honestly?

options.a: Widen the enum with each new currency as it appears in a document
options.b: Turn the enum into free text so that nothing can ever be refused
options.c: Map values that are not covered to the nearest covered value
options.d: Add unclear for the silent case, and other with a detail field for new values

explanation.d: The page gives the pair (module 62, page 1): "`other` plus a detail field for a value the enum did not foresee".
explanation.a: Ruled out because widening hides the question: "Both beat the alternative of widening the enum for every new value, which hides the question of whether the value matters."
explanation.b: Ruled out because free text cannot be compared: "with closed enums for category and severity it makes the policy computable"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a closed set forces a choice: "A closed enum forces a choice even when the document is silent or the value is new."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A dashboard reports 97 percent among the records that were accepted, yet a tenth of the clients' uploads broke and never reached the next system. Which base should the figure use?

options.a: Only the accepted records that reached the next system
options.b: All inputs that arrived, each one lost on the way scored as wrong
options.c: A mean taken over the kinds of input, so that rare kinds count equally
options.d: Only the records that a person reviewed by hand

explanation.b: The page defines it (module 75, page 1): "A document that failed is a document the customer sent."
explanation.a: Ruled out because validated records alone flatter the run: "The figure on the validated ones alone is a different figure and is always at least as high."
explanation.c: Ruled out because an average hides weak kinds: "an average over easy documents"
explanation.d: Ruled out because reviewed records are a subset: "The accuracy of a run is the share of all documents whose delivered record is correct."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A pipeline handles invoices, receipts and credit notes, each with its own extraction tool, and the model allows forcing. Which setting fits?

options.a: The option that demands a call but lets the system pick which one
options.b: A named choice of the invoice extraction entry alone
options.c: Automatic choice, leaving the model free to answer in text
options.d: No tools at all, with the answer parsed from prose by a regular expression

explanation.a: The page states it (module 62, page 2): "On a model that supports forcing, a pipeline with several document types uses `any`, and a pipeline with one type may name it."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a named tool fixes one choice: "One particular tool must be the call of this request"
explanation.c: Ruled out because automatic choice guarantees nothing: "Nothing: it may answer in text"
explanation.d: Ruled out because prose is not a status: "a decision made on prose is a guess"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A team makes every field of an invoice schema nullable, to be safe. Reviewers say that a fully optional schema feels safer because nothing can be rejected. What is the cost?

options.a: Nothing, as every field still arrives in the result
options.b: Required entries check more, so null fits only absent values
options.c: Parsing fails whenever one of the fields is left empty or missing
options.d: The model stops filling any entry with real data at all

explanation.b: The page states it (module 62, page 1): "Do not make every field nullable; nullability is for values that can really be absent, since a required field with a valid value is a stronger check."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page names the cost as lost checking: "a required field with a valid value is a stronger check"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a field may be missing from the source and then be nullable: "a field that may be missing from the source is optional or nullable"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the remedy has a limit: "nullability is for values that can really be absent"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. Two chunks of one document give the vendor as null in the first and as a name with a quote in the second. How does the merge treat that field?

options.a: It keeps the earliest usable entry, with its passage
options.b: It keeps null, as the first chunk came first in the document
options.c: It marks a conflict and asks a person to resolve it by hand
options.d: It joins both into one string separated by a comma and a space

explanation.a: The page states the rule (module 62, page 2): "keep the first value that is neither null nor unclear, with the quote it came with".
explanation.b: Ruled out because null means the source did not state it: "a field that may be missing from the source is optional or nullable"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a conflict needs two real values: "when a later chunk gives a different vendor or total, do not pick silently"
explanation.d: Ruled out because only line items are joined: "concatenate the line items"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. In a sample of accepted extractions, one wrong item fits no known pattern of mistakes. What does it signal?

options.a: A known weakness, to be logged and then ignored by the team
options.b: Noise from random sampling, which more samples will average out later
options.c: A reviewer slip, to be corrected by a second reviewer afterwards
options.d: A new kind of fault, which is the cue to change the pipeline

explanation.d: The page states it (module 68, page 1): "a wrong item that fits no known pattern is a novel error, which is the signal to change the pipeline".
explanation.a: Ruled out because new kinds appear when formats change: "the true error rate among accepted items is unknown, and new kinds of error appear when document formats change"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the sample does two jobs: "Checking the accepted sample does two jobs."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a single pull says almost nothing about hard strata: "A single random pull from the whole stream is mostly easy cases and says almost nothing about the small, hard strata."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. On a labelled set, a team wants the precision of automation at a candidate confidence cut-off of 85. How is it measured?

options.a: Average the confidence values of the items that fall below 85 on the set
options.b: Take the items just under 85 and count how many of them are wrong
options.c: Take every item at or above 85 and see what share of them is right
options.d: Sample the accepted items by stratum and take the mean of the sample

explanation.c: The page states it (module 68, page 1): "For a candidate threshold, take every item at or above it, and measure how many are right. This is the precision of automation at that threshold."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the first step groups by confidence: "Group the labelled items by the confidence they were given."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the choice comes after the measurement: "Pick the lowest threshold whose precision reaches the target."
explanation.d: Ruled out because stratified sampling is a different job: "The sample must be random within each stratum"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A hook that must replace what the model sees as a tool's output has to work for built-in tools and for MCP tools, in both SDKs. Which field should it set?

options.a: additionalContext, since it overwrites the whole result with the text that is given
options.b: The newer successor setting, since the older one is limited to one server type and is deprecated
options.c: updatedInput, since it rewrites the call before the model reads the answer
options.d: permissionDecisionReason, since the model reads that text in place of the actual result

explanation.b: The page names the field (module 49, page 2): "To replace the tool's output before Claude sees it, set `updatedToolOutput`, which works for any tool in both SDKs."
explanation.a: Ruled out because that field is for adding: "to append information to the tool result"
explanation.c: Ruled out because that field changes the call, not the result: "A replacement input for the tool"
explanation.d: Ruled out because that text appears only on a refusal: "for a denial it is what the model reads"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. An adaptive loop halts when its planner issues a step it has already run. After a while the planner re-issues the step with different capitalisation. How should the check treat it?

options.a: Compare the exact bytes, since any difference between two steps shows real progress
options.b: Ignore case and surrounding spaces, since a faltering one seldom copies itself byte for byte
options.c: Compare only the first word of each step, since the rest is only detail
options.d: Skip the check altogether and rely on the step limit alone to end the run

explanation.b: The page states it (module 50, page 2): "the repeated-step check ignores case and outer spaces, because a planner that has been stuck rarely repeats itself byte for byte".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the status names the cause: "The plan has stopped making progress"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the planner is the only judge of success: "The only success; the summary is the planner's"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the limit counts steps and the check counts repeats: "The planner is asked once more after the last allowed step"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. An Edit call is refused because the target text appears three times in the file, and only one of the places should change. What is the first remedy?

options.a: Set replace_all, which changes just the line that was meant and no other
options.b: Read the file again and then retry the identical call
options.c: Use Read and Write to rewrite the whole file
options.d: Lengthen the anchor string until just the intended spot matches

explanation.d: The page orders the remedies (module 56, page 1): "A longer anchor changes only the occurrence you meant."
explanation.a: Ruled out because replace-all is for renames: "`replace_all` changes every occurrence, which is right for a rename and wrong when only one of three similar lines should change."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a second read does not change the match count: "The order of remedies is the order of risk."
explanation.c: Ruled out because rewriting is the last resort: "which is the guide's fallback, changes the file by rewriting all of it"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A developer has a deploy skill in ~/.claude/skills and the repository has its own deploy skill. Both places hold a skill called deploy, and the developer types the slash command without any prefix. Which one runs on /deploy?

options.a: The repository's, since committed files always override personal ones on every machine that uses the project
options.b: Neither, since a name clash disables both of them until one is renamed
options.c: Both, one after the other, starting with the committed one
options.d: The home-folder one, because that location outranks the committed one for a shared name

explanation.d: The page gives the order (module 58, page 1): "Enterprise over personal, and personal over project."
explanation.a: Ruled out because personal outranks project: "so a personal skill with the team's name silently replaces the team's version on your machine"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a clash has a winner: "`/deploy` runs the personal one"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the rule is about skills that share a name: "Of skills that share a name"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A team rule seems ignored in a session. Which command shows what instruction files actually loaded?

options.a: /context, since an entry missing from its list cannot be seen by the model
options.b: /memory, which lists the files that loaded and the ones that were skipped, with the reason for each
options.c: /clear, which reloads every file from disk
options.d: /compact, which prints the instructions that survive summarising

explanation.a: The page names the command (module 57, page 1): "`/context` lists the memory files that loaded into the session".
explanation.b: Ruled out because that command lists locations and opens them: "`/memory` lists the memory file locations and opens them in your editor, including ones you have not created yet."
explanation.c: Ruled out because clearing starts again and does not report: "Run `/clear` and start again"
explanation.d: Ruled out because compaction replaces text: "Compaction replaces older messages with a summary"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A developer approves a plan in plan mode and picks the option that auto-accepts edits. Which two statements describe what approval does to the session? (Select two.)

options.a: It applies the plan to a copy of the repository before touching the real files
options.b: It adopts the permission setting that the selected choice names
options.c: It ends the read-only phase
options.d: It restarts the session with the plan as its first message
options.e: It stays in plan mode and queues the edits until the end of the session

explanation.b: Approving "exits plan mode and switches the session to the permission mode each approve option describes" (module 59, page 1).
explanation.c: Approving "exits plan mode and switches the session to the permission mode each approve option describes" (module 59, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Reading is free, and shell commands are controlled by the session".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "approve and start editing (in auto mode, or auto-accepting edits, or approving each edit by hand)".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "In plan mode Claude researches and proposes, and does not change your source."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A developer asks Claude to write the code and then its tests from that code. The session produced twelve tests that all pass at once. Why is that weak?

options.a: Tests written after the code run more slowly than tests written before it was started by the team
options.b: Claude cannot write tests for code that it wrote itself earlier in the same session
options.c: Generated tests are rejected by the runner unless a person has signed them off first
options.d: Cases born of one misreading confirm nothing, so the first checks should come from a person

explanation.d: The page states it (module 59, page 2): "A test written from the same misunderstanding as the code verifies nothing, which is why the first test cases come from a person or from the examples, and not from the code under test."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the loop is the strength of tests: "Claude does the work, runs the check, reads the result, and iterates until the check passes."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a check Claude can run is the aim: "Give Claude a check it can run: tests, a build, a screenshot to compare."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the developer writes or commissions them first: "The developer's part is to write, or have Claude write, the tests first and to give the target as the failing tests."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A skill's description and when_to_use text together run to several thousand symbols. What happens in the skill listing?

options.a: The skill is dropped from the listing until the wording is shortened by its author
options.b: They are cut at 1,536, so the key use case belongs first
options.c: Only the description is shown and when_to_use is discarded from the listing
options.d: A model call summarises the wording before the skill is listed for use

explanation.b: The page states it (module 58, page 1): "It should say what the skill does and when to use it, with the key use case first".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the text is used to decide: "Claude uses this to decide when to apply the skill"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the description is the only thing in context: "For a skill Claude may invoke, the description is the only thing in context until it loads"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the cut is a fact, not a removal of the skill: "is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A team has a repeatable procedure that should only enter context when someone starts it. Where does it belong?

options.a: In a project skill, whose body loads only when it is invoked
options.b: In the root memory file, which loads at launch
options.c: In a scoped rule with a paths list, which loads on a match between the files of the project
options.d: In the settings file as a hook that runs at session start

explanation.a: The page gives the table (module 58, page 2): "Its body loads only when invoked".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the root file is for every task: "Needed in every task of the project"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a scoped rule is for a kind of file: "About one kind of file, wherever it sits"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a hook is for fixed points: "it runs at a fixed point, whether or not the model remembers"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A developer wants short answers in every project on their machine, and the team does not. Where does that preference go?

options.a: In the project's root memory file, committed so that the whole team receives it
options.b: In a local note beside the root file, ignored by version control on every machine
options.c: In the user-level memory document or the user rules folder in the home directory
options.d: In the managed policy file that the organisation distributes to its machines

explanation.c: The page states it (module 57, page 2): "A preference that follows you into every project, such as short answers, goes in the user file or in `~/.claude/rules/`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a committed file is for the team: "Two kinds of line do not belong in a committed file."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a local note is for one project: "A note about one project that nobody else needs, such as a sandbox address, goes in `CLAUDE.local.md`"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a managed file reaches everyone: "Everyone on the machine, and individual settings cannot exclude it"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A developer asks Claude to refactor a module, and the session ends with code that looks finished but breaks a test. The prompt asked only to clean up the module and gave no further instruction. What was missing?

options.a: A longer prompt describing the module in much more detail than before
options.b: A higher thinking budget so that the model reviews its own work harder
options.c: A second conversation that reviews the refactor once the session is over and reports back to the team
options.d: A runnable check, since otherwise an appearance of completion is the only signal

explanation.d: The page states it (module 71, page 2): "Give Claude a check it can run: tests, a build, a screenshot to compare."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the model stops when the work looks done: "Claude stops when the work looks done"
explanation.b: Ruled out because more room is not a new starting point: "a larger thinking budget, which gives the model more room to reason from the same starting point"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a second review in the same conversation shares the context: "a second review in the same conversation, which adds a third reader who shares the first two readers' context"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A review prompt holds standards, a few samples and the material under review. Which two statements describe the order? (Select two.)

options.a: Everything is interleaved, with each sample beside the part it resembles
