options.b: The material goes first, so the model reads the input before any instruction
options.c: Samples come first, then the material, with the standards in a footer
options.d: Rules lead, followed by worked cases each in its own tag
options.e: The input to judge sits last

explanation.d: "Examples sit between the criteria and the input, each in its own tag, with the diff last" (module 61, page 2).
explanation.e: "Examples sit between the criteria and the input, each in its own tag, with the diff last" (module 61, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "`<examples>` with one `<example>` per case, then `<diff>`".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Structure helps the model tell instructions from examples from data".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The practice asks for the order criteria, examples, diff last, and its tests check it".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A batch finishes with some entries succeeded, some expired, and one rejected as an invalid request. What is the sound reaction?

options.a: Resubmit the whole batch so that the results stay consistent with one another
options.b: Resubmit all the failures unchanged, since errors of this kind are transient
options.c: Keep the completed ones, resend the timed-out ones as they were, repair the faulty one
options.d: Discard the batch and run all of the work synchronously instead

explanation.c: The page lists the reactions (module 63, page 1): "An entry that expired, was canceled, or hit a server error is resubmitted unchanged in the next batch".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a full resubmission pays twice: "Resubmitting the whole batch pays twice for work that is done."
explanation.b: Ruled out because an invalid entry fails again: "sending it again fails again"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the discount is worth keeping: "The half price is a reason to move work that can wait."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A bulk job submits batch entries that set stream to true. What happens?

options.a: Results stream back entry by entry as they finish, within the window of the batch
options.b: The flag is ignored and results arrive after the window has closed
options.c: It is refused with a validation error, since results come back as one file
options.d: The batch is accepted but billed at the full price of the live API

explanation.c: The page lists it (module 63, page 1): "Three parameters are refused with a validation error: `stream: true` (the results come back as one file, not a stream)".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the results come back as one file: "the results come back as one file, not a stream"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a batch finishes within a window: "A batch finishes within 24 hours (usually much sooner)"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the discount applies to work that can wait: "The half price is a reason to move work that can wait."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A team proposes to log every tool result into the notes file during an exploration. Why is that wrong?

options.a: A file cannot be read back into a session once it has been written
options.b: Notes files are loaded into every session like an instructions file is
options.c: Working memory should hold findings, not a transcript, which is what filled the window
options.d: Tool results contain nothing that is worth keeping for later questions

explanation.c: The page states it (module 67, page 1): "it is not a transcript, which is the thing that filled the window in the first place".
explanation.a: Ruled out because later questions begin by reading it: "Later questions begin by reading the scratchpad"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the instructions file is another thing: "It is not a replacement for the project's instructions file, which holds what is true of the project for every session"
explanation.d: Ruled out because reading is what fills the window: "Exploration is the most context-hungry thing an agent does."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. On Wednesday an engineer wants to carry on Monday's exploration of the payments module as a single line of work, although two other sessions have run in that directory since. Which control fits?

options.a: Resume that session by its id, which adds to the original and keeps one thread
options.b: Fork the session, since a fork keeps the whole history and carries on the work
options.c: Continue the most recent session, which takes the newest one whatever it is
options.d: Start fresh with a prompt that asks the model to recall Monday from memory

explanation.a: The page separates the two (module 51, page 1): "Resume to continue one thread; fork to branch it."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a fork starts a second line: "a fork creates a new session with its own id, so the line of work now exists twice"
explanation.c: Ruled out because continue takes the newest: "Picks up the most recent session in the current directory and adds to it"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the history is what holds the earlier analysis: "A session is the conversation history the SDK accumulates while your agent works."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. Two forks of one session each try a refactor in the same working directory. Which two statements follow the page? (Select two.)

options.a: A comparison that must not collide gives each branch its own copy of the code
options.b: Each fork gets a private copy of the whole directory, so the attempts are isolated
options.c: Branching copies the conversation and not the disk
options.d: Their edits are merged automatically when the sessions end
options.e: The second fork is rejected at once, since a directory admits one branch

explanation.a: "Forking branches the conversation history, not the filesystem", and "For a comparison that must not collide, fork for the analysis and let each branch work in its own copy of the code" (module 51, page 1).
explanation.c: "Forking branches the conversation history, not the filesystem", and "For a comparison that must not collide, fork for the analysis and let each branch work in its own copy of the code" (module 51, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "If a forked agent edits files, those changes are real and visible to any session working in the same directory."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Forking the session without isolating the files leaves both attempts editing the same checkout".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "Two forks that each try a refactor in the same working tree write over each other."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A service runs an exploration on one machine, and an engineer wants to continue it on a CI worker. What limits this?

options.a: Sessions can be resumed only by the account that created them, whatever host is used
options.b: A saved session expires after one hour of idleness and cannot be reopened
options.c: Only the Agent SDK can resume sessions, never the command line
options.d: Saved conversations stay on the host that wrote them, so copy them or use a digest

explanation.d: The page states it (module 51, page 1): "Session files are local to the machine that created them."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the limit is the machine and not the account: "You can resume from another directory on the same machine"
explanation.b: Ruled out because idleness only changes the cost: a session "has been inactive for more than about an hour and is over 100,000 tokens"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the command line can resume SDK sessions: "You can still resume one by passing its session ID to `claude --resume <session-id>`."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A process died while a tool call was running, and the session is resumed. What does the model see?

options.a: The operation flagged as interrupted before its outcome was stored, to verify
options.b: The call is finished again silently when the session resumes, without any notice
options.c: The call is shown as succeeded, since the process had already started it
options.d: The history is cut at the last completed message and the session carries on as normal

explanation.a: The page states it (module 51, page 2): the model "is told to check whether it took effect before running it again".
explanation.b: Ruled out because nothing runs again: "doesn't finish or run again when you resume"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a session does not mark old results: "Nothing in the session marks the old tool results as old."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a session holds the conversation and not the world: "Sessions persist the conversation, not the filesystem."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A team denies Write(secrets/**) to keep the agent from changing a folder. Why does that protect nothing?

options.a: Deny rules apply only to shell commands and are not applied to any of the file tools
options.b: Folders that hold credentials are exempt from deny rules for reading and for writing
options.c: Deny rules are advisory, and the model may decide to ignore them when it sees fit
options.d: Path checks for modifications use the edit spelling, so a rule spelled the other way is never used

explanation.d: The page states it (module 56, page 2): "a `Write(path)` rule is never matched by the file permission checks".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the edit rules do cover file tools: "rules govern all built-in tools that write files"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a read deny is the strongest rule for such a folder: "A `Read` deny is the one rule that stops reading, searching and writing."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a deny is enforced by the harness, and what is not matched is the spelling: "Bash rules are matched as written."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A team screens an agent's output for dangerous calls and runs it unattended whenever the screen is clean. Which two statements apply to relying on this alone? (Select two.)

options.a: Detection covers only what its authors anticipated, so a disguise slips past
options.b: Running it on every proposal costs too much, so it must be sampled
options.c: A clean result proves nothing about what the output declares
options.d: Machine-written output cannot be read by any automatic check
options.e: It still earns its place by refusing the obvious and checking what was declared

explanation.a: "A scan finds what its authors thought of: a call spelled differently, built from strings or imported by name slips past it", yet "it refuses the obvious, it compares what the code does with what the proposal declares" (module 77, page 1).
explanation.e: "A scan finds what its authors thought of: a call spelled differently, built from strings or imported by name slips past it", yet "it refuses the obvious, it compares what the code does with what the proposal declares" (module 77, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "and it costs nothing".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "it compares what the code does with what the proposal declares".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The gate in this module does read the code".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A tool design whose name breaks the required form also declares an effect that needs a person's sign-off. What should happen first?

options.a: It goes straight to the person, who can fix the name while approving
options.b: It returns for revision, so approval goes to something worth reading
options.c: It is refused outright, with no chance of revision at all
options.d: It is approved outright and fixed at a later review of the tool

explanation.b: The page states it (module 77, page 2): "A revision comes before a gate, because a person should be asked to approve a proposal that is worth reading".
explanation.a: Ruled out because revision comes first: "A revision comes before a gate"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a format error only sends it back: "Four things only send it back: a name that is not in the fixed form"
explanation.d: Ruled out because only a clean proposal passes outright: "Only a proposal with none of these is approved outright."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A documentation tool's description is long, with its key rule in the last paragraph. What does Claude Code do with the text?

options.a: It reads all of it, since only the first sentence is shown to the user in the list, as a rule of the product
options.b: It summarises the description with a model call when the text is very long indeed
options.c: It truncates at 2,048 characters, so critical details should sit near the beginning
options.d: It rejects the server at launch with an error message naming the limit in force

explanation.c: The page states the limit (module 55, page 2): "Claude Code truncates each tool description and each server's instructions at 2,048 characters by default".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the cut is a fact: "Descriptions and server instructions are truncated at 2,048 characters by default."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the advice follows from it: "Keep them concise, and put critical details near the start."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page names the effect: "The exam rejects the length: Claude Code truncates at 2,048 characters, so what you put last may be cut."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A skill from an installed plugin has the same folder name as a project skill. How can both be used?

options.a: The extension's is prefixed with its package label, so two commands exist
options.b: The project's overrides the plugin's one of the same name
options.c: The plugin's overrides the project's one of the same name
options.d: Neither runs until one of them is renamed to remove the clash

explanation.a: The page lists the location (module 58, page 1): "with the name prefixed by the plugin's name".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the order of precedence is for skills that share a name: "Of skills that share a name"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a plugin skill is available where it is enabled: "Where the plugin is enabled"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a name clash has a winner: "`/deploy` runs the personal one"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A user-level file and a repository-level file give conflicting style advice. Which two statements follow the page? (Select two.)

options.a: The user-level file loads last, since personal preferences are applied at the end
options.b: Loading runs from the broadest scope to the most specific
options.c: Memory is guidance with good delivery, not an override
options.d: Neither file loads, since conflicting advice is dropped
options.e: The more recently edited file loads last, since the loader sorts by time

explanation.b: The documentation lists the files "in load order, from broadest scope to most specific, so a project instruction appears in context after a user instruction" (module 57, page 1).
explanation.c: The documentation lists the files "in load order, from broadest scope to most specific, so a project instruction appears in context after a user instruction" (module 57, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the load order runs "from broadest scope to most specific", so the project file comes after the user file.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "All discovered files are concatenated into context".
explanation.e: Ruled out because the order is by scope, "from broadest scope to most specific", and not by edit time.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A skill lists disallowed-tools: Bash(rm *). What does that do while the skill is active?

options.a: It denies matching commands and keeps the shell available, since only a bare name removes it
options.b: It removes the shell from the available pool for the whole turn of the skill
options.c: It has no effect, since specifiers are ignored in the headers of skills
options.d: It blocks every command until the user sends the next message to the session

explanation.a: The page states it (module 58, page 2): "A bare tool name like `Bash` removes the tool from Claude's context entirely".
explanation.b: Ruled out because only a bare name removes a tool: "only a bare name removes a tool"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a scoped entry has an effect: "a scoped entry such as `Edit(src/**)` is a narrower rule that leaves the tool in place"
explanation.d: Ruled out because patterns are exact: "The patterns in `allowed-tools` are as exact as the rules in module 38"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A developer wants the built-in exploring subagent to dig deeply into a tangled module. What can the caller request?

options.a: A level of thoroughness, from quick through medium to very thorough
options.b: A write permission, from none to full access to the whole tree of the project
options.c: A larger window, from standard to extended for the long search
options.d: A count of files to read, from ten up to a thousand files

explanation.a: The page states it (module 67, page 1): "The caller can ask for a thoroughness (quick, medium or very thorough)."
explanation.b: Ruled out because it is read-only: "with Write and Edit denied"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the cost of reading is the window: "Exploration is the most context-hungry thing an agent does."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the question has to be specific: "The question must be specific"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A large exploration moves from mapping modules to tracing flows. How should the findings of the first phase reach the second?

options.a: A digest from the notes goes into the opening prompts of the later workers
options.b: Pass the full transcript of the first phase to each second-phase worker so that nothing is lost
options.c: Let the second phase rediscover them, since fresh eyes avoid bias
options.d: Keep the first phase's workers running and reuse their windows

explanation.a: The page states it (module 67, page 1): "The coordinator summarises the first phase's findings (from the scratchpad) and puts that summary into the initial prompts of the second phase's subagents."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the transcript is what filled the window: "It does not get the old transcript, which is what filled the first window."
explanation.c: Ruled out because one phase starts from the next: "The findings of one phase are the starting point of the next."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a worker does not inherit anything: "the brief must carry what the subagent needs, because it does not inherit the conversation"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A manager tells a helper to explore the whole repository and gets back a long account. Which two statements describe what delegation needs? (Select two.)

options.a: The question has to be specific
options.b: The brief carries what the worker requires, since it inherits no conversation
options.c: The helper's window is too small for such a long search
options.d: The helper needs write access so that it can keep notes
options.e: The summary should be requested as a table instead of prose

explanation.a: "The question must be specific", and "the brief must carry what the subagent needs, because it does not inherit the conversation" (module 67, page 1).
explanation.b: "The question must be specific", and "the brief must carry what the subagent needs, because it does not inherit the conversation" (module 67, page 1).
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Subagents run in separate context windows".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "with Write and Edit denied".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "the coordinator has gained nothing".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A coordinator runs five sources in order, and the second fails with a timeout. The run stops there. What does that waste?

options.a: Everything scheduled after the broken one, whose work was never done
options.b: Only the failed source's partial results, which were small anyway and a little context
options.c: Nothing, since later sources depend on the second one
options.d: The retry budget, which is reset by stopping

explanation.a: The page states it (module 66, page 1): "aborting on the first failure throws away every source after the failing one".
explanation.b: Ruled out because partial results are work already done: "Discarding them wastes work the subagent did"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a failed topic does not end the plan: "There is no entry that ends the run."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a transient failure is the worker's to retry: "A transient failure, a timeout or a brief outage, is the subagent's to retry"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A normalising hook runs twice on the same result, for instance when a result is replayed. Which property should it have?

options.a: Determinism across tools: the same date shape is applied to each field that it sees
options.b: Statelessness: it must not read the tool input of the call that it handles
options.c: Idempotence: an already readable value is left alone and the answer stays empty
options.d: Atomicity: it must write the fields together or not write any of them

explanation.c: The page lists the rule (module 49, page 2): "A value that is already readable is not touched".
explanation.a: Ruled out because changing everything is the opposite of the rule: "Change only what you understand."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a hook reads the input and the id that ties events together: "the tool use id that ties a pre and a post event together"
explanation.d: Ruled out because unknown fields pass: "Fields that are not in the table pass through as they were."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A team registers a hook with the matcher Write|Edit. How is that value read?

options.a: As a regular expression that also matches names containing either word in the middle
options.b: As a list of two exact tool names, because it holds only letters and a pipe
options.c: As a path filter for the locations that those tools write to disk
options.d: As a request to match both names only when they occur in the same turn

explanation.b: The page gives the syntax (module 49, page 1): "A value with only letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, spaces, commas and pipes is read as an exact name or a list of exact names".
explanation.a: Ruled out because only other values are expressions: "anything else is read as a regular expression"
explanation.c: Ruled out because matchers see names and nothing else: "Matchers only match tool names, not file paths or other arguments."
explanation.d: Ruled out because no matcher means every event: "Hooks without a matcher run for every event of that type"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A fan-out runs one extraction pass per document, then a cross-check pass over their summaries. One of twelve passes fails. What should the run do?

options.a: Abort the whole run, since one failure makes the rest unreliable
options.b: Log it with its message, carry on with the rest, and exclude it from the last step
options.c: Retry that one forever until it succeeds, then continue
options.d: Give the last step an empty summary for it, so that the count stays complete in the report

explanation.b: The page states it (module 50, page 2): "The practice records it (path and message) and goes on with the others, and it leaves the failed file out of the cross pass."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a failure belongs to its item: "a failure in one is a fact about that file"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a loop with no bound never ends: "A loop with no bound turns a service outage into a run that never ends."
explanation.d: Ruled out because only reviewed items reach the last pass: "The cross pass sees only the files that were reviewed"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. Logs of an extraction agent show many redundant tool calls and few errors. What does the article suggest?

options.a: Rewrite the descriptions with clearer examples
options.b: Remove half of the tools so that fewer calls are possible
options.c: Raise the output ceiling so that each call returns more
options.d: Rightsize the pagination or token limit parameters

explanation.d: The page quotes the article (module 52, page 2): "Lots of redundant tool calls might suggest some rightsizing of pagination or token limit parameters is warranted".
explanation.a: Ruled out because errors, not repeats, point at descriptions: "lots of tool errors for invalid parameters might suggest tools could use clearer descriptions or better examples"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the article warns about overlap and not about a count: "Too many tools or overlapping tools can also distract agents from pursuing efficient strategies."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a response should be lean: "Design tool responses to return only high-signal information."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. An extraction tool looks up a vendor record by its number, and the call times out. Which handling does the page give?

options.a: Send it again only after the vendor service confirms the first call did not run
options.b: Treat the timeout as proof that the record does not exist
options.c: Send it again, since repeating a read changes nothing
options.d: Send it once more with a new record number, so that attempts are told apart

explanation.c: The page gives the rule (module 53, page 2): "Repeating a read changes nothing, so a timed out lookup can simply be sent again."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a read needs no confirmation: "Repeating a read changes nothing"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a timeout carries no news: "A timeout after sending is not a failure of the effect; it is the absence of news."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the number is the lookup key: "so a timed out lookup can simply be sent again"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. An extraction stores for each field the quote it came from. What does a passing check prove?

options.a: That the value is correct, whatever the text says
options.b: That the model is confident about the value it gave
options.c: That the schema is valid for the document type
options.d: That the value is grounded in the text, not that it is correct

explanation.d: The page limits the check (module 62, page 1): "Provenance does not prove a value is correct, only that it is grounded".
explanation.a: Ruled out because other checks cover correctness: "the sum check and the review of conflicts cover the rest"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the test is plain code: "it does not ask the model whether it is right"
explanation.c: Ruled out because provenance is part of the shape: "a required `provenance` object that maps each field to a quote"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A schema gives a missing vendor name the default unknown. Why does that hurt downstream?

options.a: It breaks the parser of the report that reads each record
options.b: It lowers accuracy in the final report that the team reads
options.c: It forces the model to guess the vendor on every record
options.d: Code cannot tell it from a real value, so a placeholder passes as real

explanation.d: The page gives the reason (module 62, page 1): "downstream code cannot tell it from a real value".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the parse is fine: "The JSON never fails to parse."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a clean record passes: "A pipeline that stops at schema validation reports a high success rate and passes wrong records on."
explanation.c: Ruled out because nullability is the remedy: "a field that may be missing from the source is optional or nullable"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A team plans a weekly extraction over thousands of stored documents and wants the lowest cost. Which two statements describe the right approach and its entries? (Select two.)

options.a: The synchronous interface in parallel threads fits, since discounts need a contract
options.b: Batch processing with stream set to true fits, so that results arrive one by one
options.c: The synchronous interface with streaming fits, since results arrive sooner
options.d: The queued interface fits, since the work can wait
options.e: Each entry carries a unique identifier, as results return in any order

explanation.d: "A batch entry is `{custom_id, params}`", and the `custom_id` is "the only link between a request and its result, because the results "can be returned in any order"", so the half price suits work that can wait (module 63, page 1).
explanation.e: "A batch entry is `{custom_id, params}`", and the `custom_id` is "the only link between a request and its result, because the results "can be returned in any order"", so the half price suits work that can wait (module 63, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The half price is a reason to move work that can wait."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the results come back as one file, not a stream".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Standard documents go to the batch queue".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A pipeline's overall accuracy clears its target, and the team proposes dropping manual review for everything. What does the page say decides this?

options.a: The overall average, since a figure above target covers every kind
options.b: Evidence for each kind of input, never the average
options.c: The workload that reviewers face in a normal week
options.d: The model's own confidence on each record it returns

explanation.b: The page states it (module 75, page 1): "decided by evidence for each kind, never by the average."
explanation.a: Ruled out because an average can hide a hopeless kind: "The dashboard says 99 percent and the reviewers say handwriting is hopeless"
explanation.c: Ruled out because a workload is not evidence: "decided by evidence for each kind"
explanation.d: Ruled out because confidence is not the test: "The status is derived from the checks, and the model's own opinion plays no part."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A record has the currency other and no currency_detail. How does the pipeline classify it?

options.a: As a semantic error, since the value is plausible but unchecked
options.b: As a syntax error, because the pair is the contract
options.c: As valid, since other is a member of the enum
options.d: As an absent value that goes straight to review untried

explanation.b: The page states it (module 62, page 1): "A record with `other` and no detail is a syntax error, because the pair is the contract."
explanation.a: Ruled out because semantic errors are about meaning: "a vendor in the currency field"
explanation.c: Ruled out because other comes with its detail: "`other` plus a detail field for a value the enum did not foresee"
explanation.d: Ruled out because absence is another case: "A required value that the model reports as absent is not retried: the document goes to review"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A batch's results file lists entries in a different order from the requests. How should the pipeline pair each result with its request?

options.a: By position, since results mirror the sequence in which the entries were sent to the batch service
options.b: By matching the text of each answer against the text of each prompt sent
options.c: By the unique label that each submission carries, because sequence is not promised
options.d: By timestamps, since the earliest request normally finishes first

explanation.c: The page states it (module 63, page 1): "it is the only link between a request and its result".
explanation.a: Ruled out because results come in any order: "can be returned in any order"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the label is a short identifier: "The `custom_id` is 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, hyphens and underscores"
explanation.d: Ruled out because each entry has its own result: "A finished batch has a result per entry: succeeded, errored, canceled or expired."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. One pass reports the same defect twice, and another pass reports it once. How many independent confirmations are there?

options.a: Two, since a reviewer that repeats itself still counts as one voice
options.b: Three, since each report of the defect is a confirmation
options.c: One, since the second reviewer only repeats the first one
options.d: Zero, since independent confirmation needs at least three reviewers

explanation.a: The page states it (module 63, page 2): "A pass that reports it twice counts once, since repetition inside a pass is not independent evidence."
explanation.b: Ruled out because identity is by file, line and issue: "The same finding, identified by file, line and issue, reported by two passes is one finding."
explanation.c: Ruled out because independence is about the reviewer: "A reviewer is independent if it could not have copied the author's rationale."
explanation.d: Ruled out because passes produce lists that are combined by rules: "Several independent passes produce several lists."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. On a labelled set, no confidence cut-off reaches the 95% target. What follows?

options.a: Use the cut-off with the highest precision and automate everything above it
options.b: Lower the target until some cut-off qualifies for automation
options.c: Ask the model to restate its confidence on a hundred-point scale
options.d: Every item needs review until the pipeline improves, since no honest boundary exists

explanation.d: The page states it (module 68, page 1): "If no threshold reaches the target, there is no honest cut-off: every item needs review until the pipeline improves."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rule picks the lowest qualifying threshold: "The lowest qualifying threshold automates the most work while meeting the target."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a threshold has to reach the target: "Pick the lowest threshold whose precision reaches the target."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a restated number is still a score: "The number is only a score"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. A subagent cannot name a source for a statement that the schema demands one for. What should it do?

options.a: Invent a plausible citation so that the schema validates the finding
options.b: Cite the search engine as the source of each unsourced claim
options.c: Return it as a finding with an empty reference field and a warning
options.d: Report it apart as lacking an origin, or omit it, rather than return it as a finding

explanation.d: The page states it (module 69, page 1): "A subagent that cannot name a source for a statement does not return it as a finding: it reports it separately as unsourced, or leaves it out".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a required field pushes toward invention: "a required field pushes a model to invent a value when there is none"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a source travels with its claim: "A source survives as long as it travels with its claim in a field."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a finding without a source is refused on entry: "a finding without one is refused where it enters the pipeline"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6. Six extraction workers may be lost to a restart. When should each write its state file?

options.a: As it learns, so that a crash half-way still leaves something
options.b: At the end only, when its findings are complete and checked
options.c: Once an hour on a timer, whatever it has learned in that time
options.d: Only when a person asks for a checkpoint of its work

explanation.a: The page states it (module 67, page 2): "It is written as the agent learns and not only at the end, so that a crash half-way leaves something."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a crash gives no warning: "A crash does not warn."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the file holds findings in a fixed form: "holding its findings in the scratchpad form of page 1: specific, once, grouped"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the path is fixed by the design: "Each agent exports its state to a known location"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A loop checks a turn limit before every model call. On one run the limit is ten, and the tenth reply ends its turn with a full answer. Which status should a correct loop report?

options.a: Max turns, because the number of calls reached the limit on that very reply of the run
options.b: Truncated, because the loop made its last permitted request and must therefore assume that the text was cut off
options.c: Unexpected, because a loop that has no call left cannot confirm how the reply ended
options.d: Done, because the tally was tested before that last request and nothing was cut

explanation.d: The page puts the check where it protects the last call (module 45, page 1): "a reply that ends the turn on the very last allowed call is still done".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a reply that ended its turn is finished, and the count is only a backstop: "Keep the count as a backstop, above the real need, with a status that is not `done`."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a reply that ended its turn is not cut off, since the page reads that stop reason as "Claude finished its response naturally."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a known value is handled by name: "in your own code, give every other value a status of its own."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A reply that describes a refund policy ends with the stop reason `max_tokens`, in the middle of a sentence. Which two statements describe what the loop should do? (Select two.)

options.a: Call the model again at once with identical messages, since a cut-off reply is a fault of the service
options.b: Treat a higher ceiling as the code's decision
options.c: Treat the run as finished, since the model stopped producing tool calls
options.d: Leave with a status of its own, as the output is cut off
options.e: Ask the model to repeat the answer in fewer words, since the ceiling is the reply's fault

explanation.b: The page lists the value: "Leave with a status of its own: the reply is cut off, and raising the limit is a decision for your code" (module 45, page 1).
explanation.d: The page lists the value: "Leave with a status of its own: the reply is cut off, and raising the limit is a decision for your code" (module 45, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Run the calls and send the results; this is the only value that continues".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A value the loop has never seen must not be guessed at."
explanation.e: Ruled out because "The response reached your `max_tokens` limit."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A pre-call hook denies refunds above 500. The hook returns a short sentence that the model reads before it decides what to tell the customer. Which reason should it return to the model?

options.a: Forbidden by company policy for this kind of request
options.b: Amounts over that limit go to a person, so hand this case over
options.c: Permission denied for the requested action by the rules
options.d: Blocked for now: please retry the same call again in a moment or two, after a short pause

explanation.b: The page prefers a reason that teaches (module 49, page 1): a reason "tells the model what to do next, which is the same design as the refusal sentence of module 48".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a bare refusal says nothing to do: "A reason is part of the interface."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a flat denial ends the attempt: "Writing to /etc is not allowed"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the reason "tells the model why, so it avoids retrying."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A hook converts epoch seconds to dates in order results. A tool returns a plain-text error. What should the hook do?

options.a: Parse it as JSON and fill the missing fields with defaults so that the shape is uniform for the next stage
options.b: Replace it with a tidy message so that every result looks the same
options.c: Raise an exception, so that the call is retried by the loop
options.d: Pass it through unchanged with an empty answer, since rewriting it would hide the failure

explanation.d: The page limits the normaliser (module 49, page 2): "since rewriting an error hides the failure".
explanation.a: Ruled out because it changes only what it understands: "Fields that are not in the table pass through as they were."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page rejects it by name: "Normalise by rewriting every result, errors included."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a crash is not a repair: "A guard that crashes on unexpected input is therefore a guard that lets the call through."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A hook script stops a refund by signalling failure to the harness and also prints a machine-readable decision. Which two statements does the guide support? (Select two.)

options.a: Prefer the status and discard the structured output, because the status is read first
options.b: A single approach is the rule for each component
options.c: Print the structured output first and signal failure afterwards, so both are recorded
options.d: Always print the structured output too, since the status alone is ignored
options.e: Status 2 blocks with a stderr message, while status 0 with structured output gives finer control

explanation.b: The guide says "Use exit 2 to block with a stderr message, or exit 0 with JSON for structured control. Choose one approach per hook" (module 49, page 2).
explanation.e: The guide says "Use exit 2 to block with a stderr message, or exit 0 with JSON for structured control. Choose one approach per hook" (module 49, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Where the reason lands depends on the event".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the guide says to "Choose one approach per hook", and not both together.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Mixing them leaves it to the reference to say which wins, and a guard should not depend on that."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. An agent's loop answers two tool calls that came in one reply. In what shape must the results go back?

options.a: Together in one user message, with those blocks placed before any added text
options.b: In separate user messages, one per call, in the order the calls were made by the model itself
options.c: In one assistant message, since the model asked for the work
options.d: In one user message, with explanatory text first and the blocks after it

explanation.a: The page gives the shape (module 45, page 2): "the tool_result blocks must come FIRST in the content array."
explanation.b: Ruled out because one message answers the whole turn: "A turn with three calls gets one user message with three results"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the answer is a user message: "Tool result blocks must immediately follow their corresponding tool use blocks in the message history"
explanation.d: Ruled out because blocks come first: "the tool_result blocks must come FIRST in the content array."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A loop receives a reply whose stop reason is stop_sequence. The setup lists two custom endings for a generation. What should it do?

options.a: Continue with the next request, since only an end of turn means that the work is finished
options.b: Raise the output ceiling and ask again with the same messages
options.c: Treat it as finished, and check which of the configured strings fired if that matters
options.d: Report an unexpected value that needs an alert and a person to look at it

explanation.c: The page gives the action (module 45, page 1): "Leave: done, and read which sequence fired".
explanation.a: Ruled out because only one value continues: "Run the calls and send the results; this is the only value that continues"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a cut-off is another value: "Leave with a status of its own: the reply is cut off, and raising the limit is a decision for your code"
explanation.d: Ruled out because this value is known: "A value the loop has never seen must not be guessed at."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A lookup finds no orders for a customer. The customer exists, but no purchase was made in the period that was searched. Which reply is right?

options.a: An error result flagged as not found, so that the agent tries another route through the other service
options.b: An empty string, so that the agent decides what it means
options.c: A successful response saying that nothing matched the identifier and the date range
options.d: A transient error with retry set, in case the index is catching up

explanation.c: The page treats it as success (module 53, page 1): "A lookup that finds no orders for a customer has worked."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a failure and an empty answer are different: "from a valid empty result, which is a successful query that found no matches"
explanation.b: Ruled out because the two replies mean opposite things: "The two replies look alike in a log and mean opposite things"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a transient failure is a timeout or a limit: "A timeout, an unavailable service, a rate limit: the same call may work soon"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. The wrapper has no information yet about the state of the remote system. Which two of these calls may be sent again after a timeout without first checking state? (Select two.)

options.a: A refund that carries an idempotency key which the service honours
options.b: An email send, because the outbox accepted it before the timeout occurred
options.c: A ticket creation, because duplicates can be merged later
options.d: A refund with no key, because the amount is validated
options.e: A lookup that only reads a record

explanation.a: "Repeating a read changes nothing, so a timed out lookup can simply be sent again", and so can "A call that carries an idempotency key that the service honours" (module 53, page 2).
explanation.e: "Repeating a read changes nothing, so a timed out lookup can simply be sent again", and so can "A call that carries an idempotency key that the service honours" (module 53, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "an email that left the outbox cannot be called back".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a ticket created twice is two tickets".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a refund sent twice refunds twice".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A refund call fails with a permission error, and the loop retries it three times. The error text says that the caller lacks the right to issue refunds. What went wrong?

options.a: Only a person with authority settles it, so repeating puts a human question to a machine
options.b: Three is too many, and a single retry after a short pause would have succeeded
options.c: The error should have been marked as a validation failure by the tool author
options.d: The loop should have retried with a different amount each time it failed

explanation.a: The page states it (module 53, page 1): "a loop that retries a permission failure three times has asked a person's question of a machine three times".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a transient fault is the kind that clears: "A timeout, an unavailable service, a rate limit: the same call may work soon"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the two failures are repaired differently: "but the agent repairs one and escalates the other"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a validation failure is about the input: "The input was wrong: a missing field, a value out of range, a bad format"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A support agent's tools come from a billing service and a shipping service, and both define a tool named lookup. How should the names be set?

options.a: Rename them lookup1 and lookup2, since numbers keep the labels short and unique across the whole catalogue
options.b: Begin each one with the system it belongs to, so that each family is easy to tell apart
options.c: Keep both as lookup and rely on the descriptions to separate them in each turn
options.d: Merge them into one lookup that tries both of the services in turn

explanation.b: The page quotes the documentation (module 52, page 1): "When your tools span multiple services or resources, prefix names with the service (for example, `github_list_prs`, `slack_send_message`)."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a name is the first thing the model reads: "A name is the first thing the model reads."
explanation.c: Ruled out because near-identical texts leave nothing to choose by: "Two tools whose texts say nearly the same thing leave the model nothing to choose by"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a merge is a larger change: "it is a larger change than a first step needs"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. An organisation wants data-handling reminders delivered to every machine and wants a particular shell command blocked. Which pairing is right?

options.a: A managed memory document for both the text and the block
options.b: Managed settings for both the reminders and the prohibition
options.c: A managed memory file for text, managed settings for the ban
options.d: A user-level memory document for both, pushed by a login script

explanation.c: The page separates them (module 57, page 1): "blocking a tool, a command or a path is done with managed settings".
explanation.a: Ruled out because memory is context and not enforcement: "Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration"
explanation.b: Ruled out because a managed memory file is for behaviour: "A managed CLAUDE.md is for behaviour"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a user-level file is personal: "You, in every project"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A support assistant's role is set in one sentence of the system prompt. What does the documentation say about such a sentence?

options.a: It carries no weight unless a page of rules follows it
options.b: It overrides each instruction that appears later in the conversation
options.c: A brief line is enough to make a difference to focus and tone
options.d: It applies to the first reply of a session and then lapses

explanation.c: The page quotes the documentation (module 76, page 1): "Setting a role in the system prompt focuses Claude's behavior and tone for your use case. Even a single sentence makes a difference."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a persona needs little: "A persona needs a name, a manner and its limits, not a page of rules"
explanation.b: Ruled out because rules that must hold belong elsewhere: "the rules that must hold belong in the second row"
explanation.d: Ruled out because a role focuses behaviour for the use case: "focuses Claude's behavior and tone for your use case"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A support team wants a reviewer that shares none of the refund assistant's reasoning. What gives the product that building block?

options.a: A second turn in the same conversation with a stricter instruction
options.b: A larger thinking budget given to the same session
options.c: A separate helper that begins with a fresh window and hands back only a summary
options.d: A copy of the conversation passed to a new instance with the notes attached for its own reading

explanation.c: The page states it (module 63, page 1): "In Claude Code a subagent starts with a fresh context window that does not include the conversation history, the skills already invoked or the files the main agent has read, and returns only a summary."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a stricter instruction leaves the reasoning in place: "a stricter instruction in the same conversation, since the reasoning is still there"
explanation.b: Ruled out because more room is the same starting point: "a larger thinking budget, which gives the model more room to reason from the same starting point"
explanation.d: Ruled out because the reviewer gets the code and not the reasoning: "the code, and not the reasoning"

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1. A long input holds twenty order summaries and a question. Where should the question and the key facts go?

options.a: The question at the start, so that the model reads it before the summaries
options.b: The ask at the end, with a short digest of the essentials at the start
options.c: Both in the middle, where the attention of the model is strongest
options.d: The question repeated after every summary so that it is never forgotten

explanation.b: The page states it (module 64, page 1): "Put the long material first and the question last."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the middle is where findings go missing: "a long input's middle is where findings go missing"
explanation.c: Ruled out because detail goes under headers: "Organise the detail under explicit headers"
explanation.d: Ruled out because quoting before answering is another tool: "Asking the model to quote the relevant passages before answering is a fourth tool for long documents."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A team places a CLAUDE.md in the folder of its payments service and expects every session in the repository to carry its rules from the first message. Sessions that never touch that folder do not show them. What explains it?

options.a: The file loads only for sessions started by its owner, since it is a personal setting
options.b: The file loads at launch but is pushed out first when context fills, since it has the lowest rank
options.c: It loads on demand, since files in subdirectories load only when read
options.d: The file loads only when a slash command names it, since commands choose memory

explanation.c: A CLAUDE.md in a subdirectory is not loaded at launch but when Claude reads files in that directory (module 71, page 1). The page's words are "Files in subdirectories load on demand when Claude reads files in those directories."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "Files in subdirectories load on demand when Claude reads files in those directories."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page names launch loading for "The root `CLAUDE.md` and the rule files without a `paths` list".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says a subdirectory file "is not loaded at launch", and nothing in it ties its loading to a command.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A repository holds a command file at .claude/commands/deploy.md and, after a refactor, also a skill at .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md. A developer types /deploy. What runs?

options.a: Both, one after the other, since the name maps to each file
options.b: The packaged definition, since it wins on a shared name
options.c: Neither, since a clash of names disables the command
options.d: The command file, since older definitions keep their place

explanation.b: Custom commands have been merged into skills, and when a skill and a command file share a name the skill wins (module 71, page 1). Existing command files keep working. The page puts it as "when a skill and a command file share a name the skill wins".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy` and work the same way".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the existing command files keep working", and the name resolves to the skill.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "when a skill and a command file share a name the skill wins".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A rule file in a project's rules folder has no paths list. The team assumes that it applies only to the files its title mentions. When does it load?

options.a: At the start of every session, since nothing restricts its scope
options.b: Never, since an unscoped rule has no target
options.c: Only when a developer names it in a command, since unscoped rules wait for a call
options.d: Only when a file of its area is opened, since rules load by relevance

explanation.a: The root file and the rule files without a paths list load at the start of every session at the same priority, so a rule meant for one area then costs context everywhere (module 71, page 1). The page puts it as "The root CLAUDE.md and the rule files without a paths list load at the start of every session, at the same priority".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the audit's finding `rule-loads-always` reports "a rule with no `paths` list".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The root `CLAUDE.md` and the rule files without a `paths` list load at the start of every session, at the same priority."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says a rule with a `paths` list loads "when Claude works with a file that matches one of its globs", and this one has none.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A rule file for handlers lists the path pattern src/api/*.ts, and a developer opens src/api/v2/orders.ts. Does the rule load?

options.a: No, since rule files read only exact file names
options.b: Yes, since the extension alone decides the match
options.c: Yes, since a star matches any depth below the folder
options.d: No, since a lone star stays within one level

explanation.d: In a paths glob the double star crosses folders and the single star stays inside one, so src/api/*.ts misses a file one level deeper (module 71, page 1). The page's example is src/api/**/*.ts for every TypeScript file below src/api/. The page puts it as "** crosses folders and * stays inside one".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a `paths` entry is "A `paths` entry is a glob", and globs match by pattern.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page's example is "`src/api/**/*.ts` reaches every TypeScript file below `src/api/`", which needs the double star.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "`**` crosses folders and `*` stays inside one".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A repository keeps shared guidance in AGENTS.md beside its memory file, and a developer adds a CLAUDE.local.md for her notes. Afterwards the assistant stops following the shared guidance. What explains it?

options.a: Her file overrides the shared guidance line by line
options.b: Local files switch off every shared file in the repository
options.c: Only one family is read, so its sibling needs importing
options.d: AGENTS.md is read only in unattended runs

explanation.c: The local file counts as a CLAUDE.md, so Claude reads only CLAUDE.md files and AGENTS.md is skipped unless it is imported or the setting is changed (module 57, page 1). The page puts it as "reads only your CLAUDE.md files".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says Claude "reads only your CLAUDE.md files" once one exists, and nothing is merged.
explanation.b: Ruled out because only AGENTS.md is skipped, because "the local file counts as a CLAUDE.md".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the file "is skipped unless you import it or change the setting", whatever the kind of run.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A team asks for a validation function with a paragraph of description, and the output handles the main scenario but guesses at awkward values. What does the page add to the prompt?

options.a: Two or three worked pairs with expected answers, one at a boundary
options.b: A request to plan before coding, with no worked pairs shown beside it
options.c: A longer paragraph on how careful and exact the code must be
options.d: A larger model, so that it infers the awkward inputs

explanation.a: Examples of input and output give the work a target: two or three cases with their expected results say what a paragraph of description leaves open, and the page's example is one valid address, one invalid and one edge (module 71, page 2). The page puts it as "Two or three cases with their expected results say what a paragraph of description leaves open".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude stops when the work looks done", and without a check "'looks done' is the only signal available".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Two or three cases with their expected results say what a paragraph of description leaves open."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the first recommendation is "Give Claude a check it can run: tests, a build, a screenshot to compare."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. To avoid match failures, a developer tells Claude Code to rewrite the whole document for a one-line fix in an existing source file. What does the page say?

options.a: Keep the whole-file write if the file is under a hundred lines
options.b: Use the edit tool, since replacing everything lets damage slip through unseen
options.c: Use the shell with a stream editor, since it avoids both tools
options.d: Keep the whole-file write, since it never fails to match

explanation.b: Write overwrites with the full content, so an accidental change elsewhere goes unseen, and for partial changes to an existing file the page says to use Edit (module 56, page 1). The page puts it as "Write overwrites with the full content, so an accidental change elsewhere goes unseen".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page names no size rule; the reason is that "it never fails to match" is not a reason to overwrite.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "For partial changes to an existing file, use Edit."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Write overwrites with the full content, so an accidental change elsewhere goes unseen."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2. A team writes one skill for each kind of code, expecting each skill to apply by itself whenever a file of its kind is opened. What happens?

options.a: Each skill applies when its folder is opened, since folders are the unit
options.b: Each skill applies by itself, since skills watch the open files
options.c: Only the newest skill applies, since later skills outrank earlier ones
options.d: Matching a path never launches one, since scoped rules are what load by location

explanation.d: A skill is invoked, or chosen by the model from its description, and a path match does not start it, so conventions that must apply by path go in rule files with a paths list (module 71, page 1). The page puts it as "a skill is invoked, or chosen by the model from its description, and a path match does not start it".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page's rule files, not skills, carry "a `paths` list of globs".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Skills load when they are invoked or chosen, not because a path matched."
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a skill is invoked, or chosen by the model from its description, and a path match does not start it".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. Before synthesis even starts, the lead of a four-worker research team has no room left because every worker returned everything it fetched. Which change fits?

options.a: The coordinator condenses each output in its own context and keeps the summary
options.b: The synthesis agent receives every output directly, bypassing the coordinator
options.c: Each worker returns its full output split over several shorter messages
options.d: Each one saves its results outside and hands back a lightweight reference

explanation.d: Large results should not travel through the hub: subagents store their work in external systems and pass lightweight references back (module 72, page 1). The page's table names the failure "Large results passed through the hub".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the failure is "Large results passed through the hub", and condensing them there still passes them through the hub.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the hub keeps the plan and the status, and the page's fix is "Subagents store their work and pass back references".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says "Subagents call tools to store their work in external systems, then pass lightweight references back to the coordinator."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. The search agent is given a tool that writes notes to a shared drive so that findings are saved, and the report agent is given web search to check a figure. A review applies the least-privilege rule. What does it conclude?

options.a: Trim each to its own job, since each holds the other's kind of access
options.b: Both are right, since extra tools make the agents more flexible
options.c: Only the report agent is wrong, since the search agent must be able to save its findings
options.d: Both are right if each tool is logged, since logging controls the risk

explanation.a: The search agent has the web tools and nothing that writes, and the report agent writes the report and calls nothing else, so each tool set is trimmed to the job (module 72, page 1). The least-privilege rule applies to each of the four subagents. The page puts it as "The search agent has the web tools and nothing that writes".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "The search agent has the web tools and nothing that writes."
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The report agent writes the report and calls nothing else."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the least-privilege rule of module 54 "applies to each of the four", and a log acts after the privilege exists.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A search for one scope fails at first, and a retry through an alternative query later succeeds. The report's list of errors still shows the first failure. What is wrong?

options.a: The scope should be marked partial, since an error once occurred there
options.b: The retry should have been hidden from the coordinator
options.c: It should have been removed, since a newer result covered that topic
options.d: Nothing, since the list is a history of every failure that occurred

explanation.c: An error that a later result for the same scope made up for is dropped from the list of errors, since the report should list what is still wrong (module 72, page 2). The page puts it as "the report should list what is still wrong".
explanation.a: Ruled out because partial status concerns findings: "A claim is marked partial only when every finding behind it was partial".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the coordinator "decides" among alternatives, and it can decide "only if the error says what failed and what could be tried".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "the report should list what is still wrong".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A tool in a subagent's chain keeps failing, and the subagent simply stops with a generic message. The team wants the system to adapt. Which behaviour does Anthropic's article support?

options.a: End the whole run at the first failure so that nothing wrong is reported
options.b: Tell the worker about the broken step, so that it adjusts
options.c: Return an empty result marked successful so that the run continues
options.d: Hide the failure from the agent so that it keeps its plan

explanation.b: The article says "Letting the agent know when a tool is failing and letting it adapt works surprisingly well", which is why a failure comes back as a result with its type, its query and alternatives (module 72, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Send the timeout to a top-level handler that ends the whole run" is rejected, because "the scopes that worked are lost with it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "it turns a failure into a false answer, and nothing downstream can recover from a failure it was never told about".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the article's line is "Letting the agent know when a tool is failing and letting it adapt works surprisingly well."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A search subagent hits a rate limit twice and succeeds on the third try, and the team's design passes every failure up to the coordinator for a decision. What does the page recommend?

options.a: Keep passing everything up, since the coordinator sees the whole picture
options.b: Report "search unavailable" so that the report stays short
options.c: Stop the run and tell the user it failed
options.d: Handle passing faults locally, and send up only what stays unresolved

explanation.d: Transient failures are handled locally, and only what the subagent cannot resolve goes up, with what was attempted and the partial results (module 66, page 1). The page says "transient failures are handled locally".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Pass every failure up; the coordinator decides about retries" is rejected.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the coordinator cannot choose a recovery without "the failure type, the query, the partial results and the alternatives".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "terminating on a single failure throws away the work of the other subagents".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. To spare the coordinator's context, a developer lets the search and analysis subagents pass findings directly to each other. What does the page say?

options.a: Allow it, since a shorter path saves tokens for the coordinator
options.b: Route it through the hub, since that gives one place to observe
options.c: Allow it if each pair logs its exchanges to a shared file
options.d: Allow it for the analysis agent only, since it reads documents

explanation.b: All communication runs through the coordinator, for observability, one way of handling errors and control over what flows where (module 46, page 1). The page's words are "all communication runs through the coordinator".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Let the subagents pass findings to each other to save the coordinator's context" is rejected.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the reasons are "for observability, one way of handling errors and control over what flows where".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "all communication runs through the coordinator".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. To keep the writer's input short, the coordinator has the synthesis step compress all findings into prose and tells the writer to add sources afterwards. What does the page say?

options.a: It is sound for numbers only, since prose carries words well
options.b: It is sound, since short input is easier to draft from the start
options.c: Claim-origin pairs must travel on, since sentences cannot restore them
options.d: It is sound if the writer searches again for each claim

explanation.c: The sources are lost in the compression and cannot be rebuilt from prose, so the claim-source mappings travel through every step (module 69, page 1). The page puts it as "the claim-source mappings travel through every step".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "the claim-source mappings travel through every step".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Summarise the findings first; the writer will add sources later" is rejected.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the sources are lost in the compression and cannot be rebuilt from prose".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3. A report's table gives a figure with no mention of the survey behind it, and a reader later sees it disagree with an audit figure and takes it for an error. What was left out?

options.a: The method, since it is part of the finding
options.b: The reader's rank, since figures vary by audience
options.c: A rounding note, since small differences come from rounding
options.d: A longer sentence, since tables lack context by nature

explanation.a: The method is part of the finding, and without it a disagreement between a survey and an audit looks like an error (module 69, page 2). The page puts it as "the method is part of the finding".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Drop the survey method from the figure; it clutters the line" is rejected.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "without it a disagreement between a survey and an audit looks like an error".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the method is part of the finding".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. To make a ticket tool safer, a developer writes a settings rule that denies it only when the argument names a closed ticket, using a parenthesised pattern on the MCP tool. What does the rule do?

options.a: It denies the whole server, since parentheses widen the pattern
options.b: It narrows the tool to closed tickets, as path patterns narrow file tools
options.c: It asks the user for each ticket, since a pattern implies a prompt
options.d: It matches nothing, since an entry of that form is skipped

explanation.d: In a settings file a rule for an MCP tool that carries parentheses is skipped and matches nothing, so an argument pattern is not a way to narrow an MCP tool there (module 73, page 1). Allow or deny the tools by name. The page puts it as "In a settings file, a rule for an MCP tool that carries parentheses is skipped, so it matches nothing".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an argument pattern is not a way to narrow an MCP tool there".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "In a settings file, a rule for an MCP tool that carries parentheses is skipped, so it matches nothing".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a rule for an MCP tool that carries parentheses is skipped", so no prompt arises from it.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A team commits a .mcp.json whose ticket server's location is written with a fallback, and whose token is written with no fallback. A reviewer objects to the first. What is the verdict?

options.a: Sound for that field, since a non-secret entry suits a placeholder
options.b: Wrong, since expansion does not work in the url field
options.c: Right, but the token should have a default as well, for a working clone
options.d: Wrong, since a fallback in any field is a credential in the file

explanation.a: The expression with a fallback expands to the variable if it is set and to the default otherwise, and a default is right for a value that is not secret and wrong for a token (module 73, page 1). The page puts it as "A default is right for a value that is not secret, such as the ticket server's address, and wrong for a token".
explanation.b: Ruled out because expansion "works in a server's `command`, `args`, `env`, `url` and `headers`".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a default for a token would be a credential in the file".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A default is right for a value that is not secret, such as the ticket server's address, and wrong for a token".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. An engineer investigated a payments module on Monday. Overnight a colleague rewrote half of it, and on Tuesday the engineer wants to carry on. Which session choice does the page key?

options.a: Run two fresh sessions and repeat the analysis in each
options.b: Begin anew with a short summary, since old results describe files as they were
options.c: Resume Monday's session, since the model remembers the analysis
options.d: Fork Monday's session, since a branch keeps the analysis and the history

explanation.b: Tool results in an old session describe files as they were, so after an overnight refactor the page keys a new session with a short structured summary and a fresh read of the files that matter (module 73, page 2). The page puts it as "Tool results in an old session describe files as they were".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the choice is about "what the old context is worth", and repeating everything wastes the findings that still hold.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Tool results in an old session describe files as they were, and the model has no way to notice."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a fork is for "several directions" that start "from one shared analysis", not for code that changed.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A pull request changes .mcp.json to add a new server, and the reviewer treats it as a configuration tweak. What does the page say?

options.a: It is reviewed by the platform team alone, since developers cannot judge servers
options.b: It needs no review, since a configuration file cannot run code
options.c: Scrutiny like code, since entries load unprompted in unattended runs
options.d: It needs a review only if the server is remote, since local ones are trusted

explanation.c: The project's servers load without a prompt in claude -p and SDK runs, so a pull request that changes .mcp.json deserves the review of a change to code (module 73, page 1). The page puts it as "The project's servers load without a prompt in claude -p and SDK runs".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the sentence says "a pull request that changes `.mcp.json` deserves the review of a change to code".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The project's servers load without a prompt in `claude -p` and SDK runs".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The project's servers load without a prompt in" those runs, and the page makes no split between remote and local.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A team denies the shell tool for its generator agent and concludes that the agent can no longer change files outside its folder. Is the conclusion sound?

options.a: Yes, since a deny rule on one tool covers its neighbours
options.b: Yes, since all writes pass through the shell
options.c: No, but only because the agent could ask a person to approve
options.d: No, since writing to disk has separate rules that must be set too

explanation.d: Denying the shell does not limit the file tools, which have their own rules, so the generator's writes must be limited by an Edit rule for its folder (module 73, page 1). The page puts it as "Denying the shell does not limit the file tools, which have their own rules".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "For files, an `Edit` rule applies to every built-in tool that edits files".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Denying the shell does not limit the file tools, which have their own rules."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the rules are checked in the order "deny, then ask, then allow", and the file tools hold rules of their own.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A developer defines a server named github in her local scope with one address, and the committed file defines the same name with headers and another address. What does Claude Code use?

options.a: Only the highest-ranking entry, taken whole, since no merging happens there
options.b: A blend, headers from one and address from the other, since merging is the default
options.c: The committed file's entry, since a team file always outranks a personal one
options.d: Both entries, connected twice, since each source keeps its own server

explanation.a: The same name is connected once, using the entire entry from the highest-precedence source, so "The entire server entry from that source is used" (module 55, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "fields are not merged across scopes".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the order is "local, project, user, plugin-provided servers, then claude.ai connectors", so the local definition ranks above the committed one.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Claude Code connects to it once, using the definition from the highest-precedence source".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. Every integration in a team's setup is flagged to be present from the opening message of each session, on the theory that tools should always be at hand. What follows?

options.a: Costs fall, since the definitions are cached once they have been loaded
options.b: Crowded context and worse selection return, since lazy loading is bypassed
options.c: Selection improves, since the model sees every definition up front
options.d: Nothing, since definitions never count against the window

explanation.b: Loading every definition at the start brings back what tool search was avoiding: crowded context and worse selection (module 55, page 2). The page puts it as "Loading all of them at the start brings back what tool search was avoiding".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page names "crowded context and worse selection" as the cost.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Loading all of them at the start brings back what tool search was avoiding".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the product keeps definitions out of context until they are needed".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4. A team wants an exploring helper that cannot change anything and can also query the company's knowledge server, and an engineer says the built-in read-only explorer already does that. What is missing?

options.a: Nothing, since the built-in one reaches every connected server
options.b: A longer root memory file that names the server
options.c: A custom project agent whose tools include the lookup
options.d: A prompt line telling the main agent to avoid writing

explanation.c: Claude Code ships a read-only explorer itself, and a project subagent of your own is the way to give the same shape the project's documentation server too, with a tools line that lists only reading and searching tools (module 73, page 1). The page puts it as "a project subagent of your own is the way to give the same shape the project's documentation server too".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says the built-in helper "is read-only", while "a project subagent of your own is the way to give the same shape the project's documentation server too".
