explanation.b: Ruled out because "the root file loads in every session and costs context each time".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A sentence in the prompt is a request that the model weighs; the `tools` line is a list the subagent cannot go beyond."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A headless step fails with a model error, and the job is configured to re-run itself until it passes. What does the page advise?

options.a: Extend the job timeout, since a longer wait is more likely to bring success
options.b: Turn the job green with an empty result, so that the pipeline moves forward
options.c: Report the breakdown and let a person decide, since repeats add expense
options.d: Re-run until it passes, since transient faults clear on their own over time

explanation.c: When a run fails, re-running it repeats the cost with no reason to expect a different result, so the job reports the failure and a person decides (module 74, page 1). The page puts it as "When a run fails, re-running it repeats the cost with no reason to expect a different result".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A longer job timeout only lets a loop run longer."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A green job that said nothing is the failure the gate prevents".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "When a run fails, re-running it repeats the cost with no reason to expect a different result".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A review prompt defines severity levels in words only, and the team finds that mediums and lows are mixed up. What does the page add to the criteria?

options.a: A longer definition for each rating, since more words fix the boundary
options.b: A request for fewer comments overall, since fewer means less noise in the output
options.c: An instruction to be conservative and report only important issues
options.d: A worked example per rating, since it shows where the boundary lies

explanation.d: Criteria have three lists, and each severity carries one example, because the example shows the model where the line between medium and low is, which a definition alone does not (module 74, page 2). The page puts it as "the example shows the model where the line between medium and low is, which a definition alone does not".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the example shows the model where the line between medium and low is, which a definition alone does not".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A sentence that asks for more care is a request; the criteria are the case list."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the vague phrases "do not say what to leave out", so they change nothing.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. The pipeline's review step continues the very session that wrote the change, so that the context is already loaded. A reviewer asks why that is a finding. What is the reason?

options.a: Authors favour their own output, since a clean slate sharpens the check
options.b: A shared session cannot run in a pipeline, since sessions are interactive
options.c: A shared session loses the findings of earlier runs, since they are discarded
options.d: A shared session costs more tokens, since the history is billed again

explanation.a: A reviewer should not be the author: a fresh context improves code review since Claude will not be biased toward code it just wrote, so the review runs as its own session (module 74, page 2). The page puts it as "A fresh context improves code review since Claude won't be biased toward code it just wrote".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page asks that "In a pipeline that means the review runs as its own session", and does not say that sessions are interactive only.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the earlier findings are a separate need: "Giving the run the earlier findings" keeps the comments useful.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "A fresh context improves code review since Claude won't be biased toward code it just wrote."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A team runs a large review three times and keeps only the issues that two of the three runs report. Why does the page reject this?

options.a: It needs a larger window to hold three results at once
options.b: Real bugs found only occasionally would be hidden by the filter
options.c: It triples the cost without any change in what is found
options.d: It lets authors skip the review when two runs disagree

explanation.b: Keeping only what two of three runs agree on would hide real bugs that are found only now and then (module 74, page 2). The remedy that fits the cause is to divide the work into a pass for each file and an integration pass. The page puts it as "would hide real bugs that are found only now and then".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A larger context window does not fix attention quality."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says it "would hide real bugs that are found only now and then".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Run the review three times and keep what two of three runs agree on" is rejected because agreement hides a real bug.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. A script submits the overnight report to the batch interface, and an audit flags that its command lacks the headless flag. Is the finding right?

options.a: No, but only because batch jobs use a different flag for headless runs
options.b: No, since that rule covers calls starting with the CLI, not a sender
options.c: Yes, since every command in a pipeline needs the flag to run unattended
options.d: Yes, since batch jobs run through the interactive terminal tool

explanation.b: A batch job's command is a script that submits the work, so the -p rule applies to commands that start with claude and not to a script (module 74, page 1). The page puts it as "a batch job's command is a script that submits the work".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the example's audit reports `no-print-flag` for "a command that starts `claude` without `-p` or `--print`".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the `-p` rule applies to commands that start with `claude` and not to a script".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a batch job's command is a script that submits the work".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. To keep a multi-file review consistent, each file's pass is shown the findings of the previous files. What does the page say about it?

options.a: Passes stop being independent, since earlier mistakes become premises
options.b: It is wrong only for the last file, since its pass needs all of them
options.c: It is sound, since consistency needs shared memory
options.d: It is sound if the findings are summarised first, since summaries are neutral

explanation.a: Seeing earlier findings makes the passes dependent, so earlier mistakes become premises, and consistency is the job of the cross pass (module 50, page 2). The page says "the passes become dependent and the earlier mistakes become premises".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Consistency is the job of the cross pass".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Let the next file pass see the findings of the previous ones, for consistency" is rejected.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the passes become dependent and the earlier mistakes become premises".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. In a review with a pass for each file, one pass fails with an error, and the job script discards everything and starts over. What does the page advise?

options.a: Merge the failed file into the next pass
options.b: Retry the failed pass until it succeeds, however long
options.c: Report the breakage by name and let the other results stand
options.d: Discard and restart, since a partial review cannot be trusted

explanation.c: The failure is reported by file, and the rest goes on, since the other passes are valid (module 50, page 2). The page puts it as "The failure is reported by file, and the rest goes on".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the passes stay independent, since otherwise "the passes become dependent".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The failure is reported by file, and the rest goes on."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "If one file pass fails, discard the review and start again" is rejected because "the other passes are valid".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5. An audit of a pipeline flags its test-generation job for holding the edit tool, citing the rule that review jobs must only read. Is the finding right?

options.a: Yes, since writing test files is a way to change things in production
options.b: Yes, since every job in the pipeline must be read-only
options.c: No, but only because a shell tool would be worse than the edit tool
options.d: No, since that limit binds inspections alone and this task writes by design

explanation.d: A review changes nothing, so its tools are Read, Grep and Glob, while test generation writes test files and is not held to the read-only rule (module 74, page 2). The audit checks the rule only for reviews. The page puts it as "The audit checks the rule only for reviews".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The test-generation job is different on purpose: it writes test files, so it has `Edit`".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The audit checks the rule only for reviews."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the review "changes nothing, so its tools are `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`".
